hr-227.one_sentence: The Clergy Act would let clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security and Medicare taxes choose to opt back in during a two-year window.
hr-227.short: Clergy members who were approved for an exemption from Social Security and Medicare taxes on ministerial earnings, based on religious or conscientious objections, could revoke that exemption. They would file an application with the IRS by the due date of their federal income tax return for the second taxable year after December 31, 2028, which is April 15, 2031 unless an extension is obtained. The revocation could take effect in 2029 or 2030 and would be permanent. The IRS would also be required to develop a plan to inform clergy members of their eligibility to revoke prior exemptions.

hr-2270.one_sentence: The bill would exclude the value of employer-funded child or dependent care from the calculation of an eligible employee's overtime pay rate.
hr-2270.short: Under current law, overtime must be paid at one and a half times an employee's regular rate, which is an average hourly rate that includes certain pay such as commissions. This bill specifies that an employer can provide or pay for child or dependent care services without counting the value of those services in that overtime calculation.

hr-23.one_sentence: The bill would require U.S. sanctions on foreign persons who help the International Criminal Court investigate, arrest, detain, or prosecute protected individuals, and would cut off U.S. funding for the court.
hr-23.short: The bill would sanction foreign individuals and entities that assist the International Criminal Court (ICC) in investigating, arresting, detaining, or prosecuting certain people. Protected persons include U.S. individuals and entities, unless the United States is a party to the Rome Statute and consents to ICC jurisdiction, as well as citizens or lawful residents of U.S. allies that are not parties to the statute or have not consented to ICC jurisdiction. Sanctions would block visas and property and extend to immediate family members of those sanctioned. The bill would also rescind all funds appropriated for the ICC and bar future use of appropriated funds for the court.

hr-2312.one_sentence: The bill would change the federal definition of a tipped employee so that an employee's job duties no longer affect whether they qualify as tipped.
hr-2312.short: Under current federal law, employers may pay tipped employees less than the federal minimum wage if tips make up the difference, and a worker counts as tipped if they regularly receive more than $30 a month in tips. This bill would broaden the definition of a tipped employee to include any worker who receives tips and other cash wages for a work period at a rate at least equal to the federal minimum wage, regardless of their duties. The work period would be set by the employer.

hr-2478.one_sentence: The bill would let mutual fund companies and their transfer agents temporarily delay certain redemptions when they reasonably believe an older or impaired adult is being financially exploited.
hr-2478.short: The bill sets out procedures for delaying the redemption of certain securities issued by open-end investment companies, such as mutual funds, if the company or its transfer agent reasonably believes the transaction involves financial exploitation. It covers individuals age 65 or older, and adults age 18 or older who cannot protect their own interests due to a mental or physical impairment. The initial delay may last up to 15 days, with an additional 10 days after an exploitation determination, and a state regulator, administrative agency, or court may extend the period. During any delay, the amounts involved must be held in a demand deposit account, and the company must notify the Securities and Exchange Commission if it uses these procedures. The bill also directs the SEC to make recommendations to address the financial exploitation of these adults.

hr-2483.one_sentence: This bill reauthorizes and revises federal programs addressing substance use disorders, overdoses, and mental health, extending many of them through fiscal year 2030.
hr-2483.short: The bill extends and updates federal programs run mainly by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration. These cover prevention, such as drug overdose monitoring, naloxone and other overdose-reversal drugs for first responders, and fetal alcohol spectrum disorder activities. It also covers treatment and recovery, including residential care for pregnant and postpartum women, workforce training and loan repayment, and support for people in recovery, and it adds cybersecurity protections for the 9-8-8 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

hr-249.one_sentence: This bill would rename a trail bridge and a park within Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park in New Jersey after former Congressman Bill Pascrell, Jr.
hr-249.short: The bill renames the Great Falls Scenic Overlook Trail Bridge in Paterson Great Falls National Historical Park as the Bill Pascrell, Jr. Scenic Overlook Trail Bridge. It also renames Overlook Park within the same park as Bill Pascrell, Jr. Overlook Park. The park is located in Paterson, New Jersey.

hr-2493.one_sentence: This bill extends through fiscal year 2030 federal grant programs that help fund health care services and networks in rural areas.
hr-2493.short: The bill reauthorizes, through fiscal year 2030, Health Resources and Services Administration grant programs that fund health care providers in rural areas. The grants cover expanding health care services, developing integrated networks of local health care organizations, and improving the quality of services provided by small rural providers. For grants that expand services or develop networks, the bill requires the agency to ensure funds are used to meet the needs of underserved populations and to involve those populations in planning and carrying out the activities.

hr-2550.one_sentence: The bill would cancel a March 2025 executive order that removed certain federal agencies from the federal labor-management law that governs employee collective bargaining.
hr-2550.short: The Protect America's Workforce Act would nullify an executive order issued on March 27, 2025, which excluded specified federal agencies and subdivisions from the Federal Service Labor-Management Relations Statute. That statute allows federal employees to take part in collective bargaining and enforces those rights. The bill also provides that any covered collective bargaining agreement in place as of March 26, 2025, would remain in full force and effect through the agreement's stated term.

hr-26.one_sentence: The bill would bar the President from declaring a moratorium on hydraulic fracturing unless Congress first authorizes it.
hr-26.short: The bill prohibits the President from declaring a moratorium on hydraulic fracturing, a process used to extract oil or natural gas by injecting water, sand, and chemicals into underground rock under pressure, unless Congress authorizes the moratorium. It also states that Congress believes states should keep primary authority to regulate hydraulic fracturing for oil and natural gas on state and private lands.

hr-261.one_sentence: The bill would stop the Department of Commerce from requiring extra permits for certain undersea fiber optic cable work in national marine sanctuaries when a state or federal agency has already approved that work.
hr-261.short: The bill covers installing, operating, maintaining, repairing, and recovering undersea fiber optic cables inside national marine sanctuaries. Commerce could not prohibit these activities or require its own authorization if a state or federal agency has already issued a license, lease, or permit for them. The bill also lets Commerce direct the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to coordinate with other federal agencies on actions that could harm sanctuary resources and involve these cable activities.

hr-2616.one_sentence: The bill would require certain public elementary and middle schools to get parental consent before changing a student's gender-related school records or sex-based accommodations, as a condition of receiving certain federal education funds.
hr-2616.short: The bill applies to public elementary schools and schools serving only grades 5 through 8 that receive certain federal funds for elementary and secondary education. Before changing a minor student's gender markers, pronouns, or preferred name on any school form, these schools would need parental consent. The same consent requirement would apply to changing a minor student's sex-based accommodations, such as locker room or bathroom use.

hr-2659.one_sentence: The bill would create a joint federal task force, led by CISA, to coordinate agency responses to cyber threats from Chinese state-sponsored actors, including Volt Typhoon.
hr-2659.short: The bill requires the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), part of the Department of Homeland Security, to establish and lead a joint interagency task force. The task force would coordinate the efforts of agencies responsible for critical sectors, such as the Departments of Defense, Energy, and Agriculture, to detect, analyze, and respond to Chinese state-sponsored cyber actors. Participating agencies would share information with the task force, with members required to hold appropriate security clearances to access classified material. The task force would report to Congress annually for six years, with the first report due no later than 540 days after it is established.

hr-2683.one_sentence: The bill would extend U.S. export controls to cover foreign persons remotely accessing controlled items over networks such as the internet or cloud services.
hr-2683.short: The bill broadens the U.S. export control system so that it applies to remote access of items, meaning access by a foreign person through a network connection from a location other than where the item is physically located. It also covers any other form of remote access that the Department of Commerce specifies in regulations. The bill lets the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security issue licenses and impose penalties for remote access to controlled items under the existing export control law.

hr-27.one_sentence: The HALT Fentanyl Act would permanently place fentanyl-related substances as a class into Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act and apply the same penalties used for fentanyl analogues.
hr-27.short: The bill permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a class in Schedule I, the category for drugs with a high potential for abuse and no currently accepted medical value. Offenses involving these substances would carry the same quantity thresholds and penalties as offenses involving fentanyl analogues, such as a 10-year mandatory minimum prison term for 100 grams or more. The bill also creates an alternative registration process for certain Schedule I research and changes some registration requirements for research with controlled substances. It further expresses the sense of Congress agreeing with a 2018 federal district court decision that butyryl fentanyl can be considered an analogue of fentanyl.

hr-2721.one_sentence: The bill would create a two-year VA pilot program to provide headstones or burial markers for certain veterans who died on or before November 1, 1990, and were not dishonorably discharged.
hr-2721.short: The bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to set up and run a two-year pilot program that provides a headstone or burial marker, when requested, for covered veterans. Covered veterans are those who died on or before November 1, 1990, and were released or discharged under conditions other than dishonorable. Under current rules, these benefits are available only to eligible veterans who died on or after November 1, 1990. The bill also requires the VA to update the National Cemetery Administration website with the eligibility requirements.

hr-275.one_sentence: The bill would require the Department of Homeland Security to report monthly on non-U.S. nationals who attempt to unlawfully enter the country and may pose a national security risk.
hr-275.short: The Special Interest Alien Reporting Act of 2025 would require the Department of Homeland Security to issue a report every month. The report would cover non-U.S. nationals who attempt to enter the United States unlawfully and who potentially pose a national security risk. For these individuals, DHS would report the total number, their nationalities or countries of last residence, and the locations where they were encountered.

hr-276.one_sentence: The bill would rename the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America and require federal agencies to update their documents and maps to use the new name.
hr-276.short: The Gulf of America Act of 2025 would officially rename the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America. It directs federal agencies to update their documents and maps so they use the new name.

hr-28.one_sentence: This bill would bar federally funded schools and colleges from letting people whose sex at birth was male take part in athletic programs designated for women or girls.
hr-28.short: The bill treats allowing male-sex individuals to participate in women's or girls' school athletic programs as a violation of Title IX, the federal law banning sex discrimination in federally funded education. Under the bill, sex means reproductive biology and genetics at birth. Male individuals may still train or practice with these programs as long as this does not deprive any female of corresponding opportunities or benefits. The bill also directs the Government Accountability Office to report on benefits to women and girls in single-sex sports that could be lost through male participation.

hr-2853.one_sentence: The bill would expand federal criminal enforcement against organized retail and supply chain crime, including theft and resale of stolen goods, and create a temporary Homeland Security center to coordinate these efforts.
hr-2853.short: The bill broadens federal offenses involving the interstate transport, sale, or receipt of stolen goods, allowing prosecution based on the total value of stolen items over a 12-month period. It makes these offenses and theft from interstate or foreign shipments count as underlying crimes for federal money laundering charges, and allows criminal forfeiture of related property. It also adds general-use prepaid cards, gift certificates, and store gift cards to the money laundering statute. Finally, it temporarily establishes a center within the Department of Homeland Security to coordinate federal law enforcement on these crimes.

hr-2860.one_sentence: This bill would reauthorize for seven years the Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative and its advisory commission, which work to protect and restore marine waters and species in the Northwest Straits region.
hr-2860.short: The bill revises and renews for seven years the Northwest Straits Marine Conservation Initiative and its Northwest Straits Advisory Commission. These programs focus on protecting and restoring marine waters, habitats, and species in the waters of the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound, from the Canadian border to the south end of Snohomish County in Washington state. The commission would support local marine resources committees, develop restoration and protection recommendations based on science, and serve as a public forum for informal discussions about the region's marine ecosystem.

hr-29.one_sentence: The Laken Riley Act would require the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-U.S. nationals arrested for theft-related crimes and let states sue the federal government over certain immigration decisions.
hr-29.short: The bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain non-U.S. nationals who are unlawfully present or lacked required documents and who have been charged with, arrested for, convicted of, or admitted to acts that are the essential elements of burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting. It also allows state governments to seek injunctive relief from federal court over certain immigration decisions or failures that caused the state or its residents harm, including financial harm over $100. The covered decisions include releasing a non-U.S. national from custody, certain inspection and asylum-interview requirements, visa issuance to nationals of countries that unreasonably deny or delay accepting their nationals, limits on immigration parole, and failing to detain someone ordered removed.

hr-2913.one_sentence: The bill would provide assistance to Ukraine and certain European countries and impose penalties on Russia and certain foreign persons in connection with the war between Russia and Ukraine.
hr-2913.short: The bill would create a reconstruction trust fund for Ukraine, direct the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation to prioritize support for Ukraine, and extend certain defense and security assistance authorities through 2027 or 2028. It would also require the State Department to help build the militaries and border forces of Baltic countries. If the President determines that Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, refusing to negotiate in good faith, or violating a peace agreement, the bill requires sanctions on certain Russian officials, companies, and financial institutions. It would also raise the duty rate on imports from Russia to at least 500 percent of their value.

hr-2931.one_sentence: The bill would require the Small Business Administration to move any office located in a sanctuary jurisdiction to a location that is not one, and bar it from opening new offices there.
hr-2931.short: The bill requires the Small Business Administration to relocate a regional, district, or local office within 60 days if the agency publicly determines the office is in a sanctuary jurisdiction. A sanctuary jurisdiction is defined as a state or local government that prohibits or restricts officials from sharing information about an individual's citizenship or immigration status with other government entities, or from complying with specified Department of Homeland Security requests. The SBA would also be prohibited from establishing new offices in sanctuary jurisdictions.

hr-2965.one_sentence: The bill would require the Small Business Administration to ensure that the yearly small business regulatory budget, meaning the cost of federal rules to small businesses, is no greater than zero.
hr-2965.short: The bill directs the Small Business Administration to keep its annual small business regulatory budget at or below zero for each fiscal year. The budget is defined as the cost to small businesses of federal rulemaking, including the cost of issuing new rules and of modifying or repealing existing ones.

hr-2966.one_sentence: The bill would change SBA 7(a) and 504 loan applications to require applicants' dates of birth and a citizenship or lawful-status certification, and would make certain noncitizen groups ineligible.
hr-2966.short: The bill revises application requirements for the Small Business Administration's 7(a) and 504 loan programs. Applications would need to include the applicant's date of birth and a certification that the applicant or all beneficial owners are U.S. citizens, nationals, or lawful permanent residents. The bill also makes certain individuals ineligible for these loans, including asylees, refugees, people holding visas to remain in the U.S., nonimmigrants, people granted deferred action under DACA, and people without lawful immigration status.

hr-2978.one_sentence: The GUARD Act would let state, local, and tribal law enforcement use certain federal grant funds to investigate financial fraud, including scams targeting older adults, and would require federal reporting on these crimes.
hr-2978.short: The bill allows state, local, and tribal law enforcement agencies and certain federal grant recipients to use grant funds to investigate general financial fraud, elder financial fraud, and "pig butchering," a scam in which victims are gradually pressured into sending increasing amounts of money, often in cryptocurrency, into a fake investment. It also allows federal law enforcement to help these agencies and fusion centers use blockchain tracing tools. Finally, it requires the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) to report on efforts to combat these scams, including any legislative recommendations, and on current conditions and trends in these crimes across the United States.

hr-2987.one_sentence: The CEASE Act of 2025 would limit the number of for-profit small business lending companies authorized to make 7(a) loans to no more than 16 at any one time.
hr-2987.short: The bill caps the number of for-profit small business lending companies that may be authorized to make 7(a) loans at 16 at any given time. The official summary does not describe the program further or explain the reasons for the cap. The full text of the bill is not included in the material provided, so other provisions cannot be described.

hr-2988.one_sentence: The bill would require fiduciaries of employer-sponsored retirement plans to base investment decisions mainly on financial factors, with limited exceptions, and to act in participants' interests when using shareholder rights.
hr-2988.short: The bill generally requires retirement plan fiduciaries to make investment decisions based solely on pecuniary factors, meaning factors expected to have a material effect on the risk or return of an investment. Nonpecuniary factors may be considered in certain situations, such as when choosing options for participant-directed plans or when alternatives cannot be distinguished on financial factors alone. The bill also bars discrimination in selecting and retaining plan fiduciaries, counsel, employees, and service providers, and requires fiduciaries to act solely and prudently in participants' interests when exercising shareholder rights, without having to vote every proxy. It further requires specified notices for plans that let participants choose from designated investment alternatives.

hr-30.one_sentence: The bill would make certain non-U.S. nationals inadmissible or deportable based on specified sex offenses, stalking, child abuse, and domestic violence offenses.
hr-30.short: The bill makes a non-U.S. national inadmissible to the United States if the person has admitted to or been convicted of acts that meet the essential elements of crimes such as stalking, child abuse, child neglect, child abandonment, sex offenses, conspiracy to commit a sex offense, violating certain protection orders, or domestic violence. It adds grounds for deportation, making any sex offense (including crimes against minors) or conspiracy to commit one a basis for removal. It also expands the domestic violence grounds for deportation to cover physical or sexual abuse or a pattern of coercive behavior occurring within certain close relationships.

hr-3015.one_sentence: The bill would give the National Coal Council statutory authority, direct the Department of Energy to reestablish it under its November 2021 charter, and remove the requirement that it be re-chartered every two years.
hr-3015.short: The bill provides legal authority for the National Coal Council, which was created in 1984 to advise the Department of Energy on coal and the coal industry. It directs the Department of Energy to reestablish the council in line with the charter that was in effect on November 19, 2021. The bill also removes the requirement under the Federal Advisory Committee Act that the council be re-chartered every two years.

hr-3062.one_sentence: This bill sets a new federal approval process for energy infrastructure that crosses the U.S. border with Canada or Mexico, replacing the current process under existing executive orders.
hr-3062.short: The bill requires a certificate of crossing before building or operating a border-crossing facility for oil, natural gas, or electricity transmission. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission issues certificates for oil and natural gas pipelines, and the Department of Energy issues them for electric transmission facilities, each subject to deadlines set in the bill. The President would need congressional approval before revoking an existing permit for such facilities.

hr-3095.one_sentence: The bill would require the U.S. Postal Service to designate a single, unique ZIP Code for each of 74 listed communities across the United States.
hr-3095.short: The bill directs the U.S. Postal Service to give each of 74 named communities its own single, unique ZIP Code. The communities are located in many states, including California, Colorado, Florida, Indiana, Texas, and Wisconsin. The official summary lists the communities but does not describe any further details of how the designations would be carried out.

hr-3106.one_sentence: The bill would require the Department of Homeland Security to run an exercise simulating a terrorist attack during extreme cold weather and report its findings to Congress.
hr-3106.short: The bill directs the Department of Homeland Security to develop and conduct an exercise to prepare for a terrorist attack during an extreme cold weather event, such as one caused by a polar vortex. The exercise scenario must involve an attack that causes cascading effects on critical infrastructure, and it must examine how public and private entities can coordinate to reduce those effects and strengthen community resilience. Within 60 days after the exercise, the department must submit an after-action report to Congress with initial findings, plans for applying lessons learned, and any proposed legislative changes.

hr-3109.one_sentence: The REFINER Act would require the Department of Energy to have the National Petroleum Council publish a report on U.S. petrochemical refineries, covering their energy security role, expansion opportunities and risks, and recommendations to increase capacity.
hr-3109.short: The bill directs the Department of Energy to ask the National Petroleum Council to publish a report on petrochemical refineries located in the United States. The report would cover how these refineries contribute to U.S. energy security, along with analyses and projections of opportunities to expand refinery capacity and the risks they face. It would also address any federal or state executive actions that have contributed to a decline in refinery capacity, and include recommendations for increasing that capacity.

hr-3123.one_sentence: The bill sets rules for paying a veteran's VA pension that was approved before death but not paid until afterward, giving priority to a surviving spouse, children, dependent parents, and then the estate.
hr-3123.short: The bill establishes procedures for the Department of Veterans Affairs when a pension is approved for a veteran before death but paid only after the veteran dies. The unpaid amount would go first to the living spouse, then living children, then living dependent parents, and finally to the veteran's estate unless the estate would escheat to the state. To claim these accrued benefits, a claimant must file an application within one year of the veteran's death; if no application is filed in that time, the payment goes to the estate unless it would escheat.

hr-3187.one_sentence: Directs the Forest Service to convey about one acre of its land to Perry County, Arkansas, at the county's request, for public purposes such as education and youth development.
hr-3187.short: The bill would require the Forest Service to transfer roughly one acre of federal land to Perry County, Arkansas, if the county asks for it. The county would have to use the land for public purposes, such as supporting education and youth development, or the land would revert to the United States at the Forest Service's discretion. The transfer would be made without payment, by quitclaim deed, and subject to existing rights and terms the Forest Service considers appropriate. The county would pay the costs of the transfer, including the survey and required environmental and historic preservation reviews.

hr-3234.one_sentence: The bill would raise the amount of reciprocal deposits that insured banks may accept, using a tiered limit based on total liabilities, and loosen certain rating requirements for doing so.
hr-3234.short: Reciprocal deposits are large deposits split among a network of banks so that more of the money is covered by deposit insurance. The bill increases the amount institutions may accept as reciprocal deposits and sets a tiered limit based on each institution's total liabilities. It also allows institutions with CAMELS ratings of 1, 2, or 3 to qualify, where current law relies on a composite rating of outstanding or good, among other requirements.

hr-3276.one_sentence: The bill would give statutory authority to the Urban Bird Treaty Program, which supports the conservation of birds living in or migrating through urban areas.
hr-3276.short: The bill provides legal authority for the Urban Bird Treaty Program, which is run by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. The program works with communities to help conserve and manage birds that live in or pass through cities. Support can include grants administered by the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation to government agencies, community groups, and academic institutions for related activities.

hr-3351.one_sentence: The bill would exempt certain information-gathering actions by an SEC office that supports small business capital formation from the Paperwork Reduction Act's usual procedures.
hr-3351.short: The bill excludes actions taken by the Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation at the Securities and Exchange Commission from the Paperwork Reduction Act. That law normally requires federal agencies to follow specific procedures when collecting information from the public. The bill sets out some exceptions, such as requiring the office to tell people why the information is being collected, as current law already requires.

hr-3357.one_sentence: The bill would require companies with multiple classes of shares that carry different voting rights to disclose voting-related ownership information in proxy and consent solicitations.
hr-3357.short: The bill applies to companies that issue two or more classes of shares with different voting rights, such as shares with few or no votes for the public and shares with more votes for founders and executives. Under the bill, these companies must disclose in proxy or consent solicitation materials the shares and voting power held by each director, director nominee, named executive officer, and each beneficial owner holding 5% or more of total voting power. The disclosed information would cover the number of shares of all voting classes each such person beneficially owns and the amount of voting power each holds.

hr-3383.one_sentence: The bill would let closed-end funds invest more heavily in private investment funds, and bar the SEC from restricting the sale or listing of those funds' shares.
hr-3383.short: The bill allows a closed-end fund, which holds pooled assets and has a limited number of shares traded on an exchange, to increase its investment in private investment funds. It prohibits the Securities and Exchange Commission from limiting the sale or listing of securities of a closed-end fund that invests in private investment funds. The same rules would also apply to a closed-end company treated as a business development company.

hr-3394.one_sentence: The bill would let the SEC treat individuals with qualifying professional knowledge as accredited investors, allowing them to join certain private securities offerings.
hr-3394.short: The bill expands the definition of an accredited investor, the category of people who may take part in certain private securities offerings. It would add individuals the SEC determines have qualifying professional knowledge from education or professional experience. It also writes into law some existing criteria, such as a broker or investment adviser license in good standing, a specified annual salary, or a specified net worth, and directs the SEC to revise its Regulation D definition to match.

hr-3400.one_sentence: The TRAVEL Act of 2025 would let the Department of Veterans Affairs assign physicians to serve veterans in U.S. territories for up to one year, with bonuses for those physicians.
hr-3400.short: The bill authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs to assign a physician appointed in the Veterans Health Administration to serve as a traveling physician for up to one year. The physician would provide care to veterans at VA facilities in American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, and any other U.S. territory or possession. Traveling physicians would coordinate with non-VA providers when necessary to ensure coordinated care, and the VA would provide a relocation or retention bonus to these physicians.

hr-3422.one_sentence: The bill would expand the SEC's Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation to promote capital-raising options for underrepresented, rural, and disaster-affected small businesses and to coordinate with state securities regulators.
hr-3422.short: The bill expands the functions of the Securities and Exchange Commission's Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation. The office would provide educational resources and host or join events to promote ways for underrepresented small businesses, rural businesses, and businesses affected by natural disasters to raise money. It would also meet each year with representatives of state securities commissions to discuss opportunities for collaboration and coordination.

hr-3424.one_sentence: The SPACE Act of 2025 would direct the General Services Administration to work with federal agencies on sharing space in federally leased buildings and to set measurable goals for those arrangements.
hr-3424.short: The bill directs the General Services Administration (GSA) to work with federal agencies that lease buildings to better understand concerns about shared-space arrangements. GSA would develop criteria to make space sharing easier to expand and identify how special-use space could be used for sharing. The agency would also set measurable objectives, in consultation with tenants, to judge whether shared-space arrangements are successful. GSA must brief Congress on implementation within six months of enactment.

hr-3425.one_sentence: The bill would require the Federal Protective Service to improve how it tests, trains, and tracks the contract security guards who protect federal buildings, and to report on these efforts to Congress.
hr-3425.short: Within one year, the Federal Protective Service would set up performance testing and improvement rules for contract security personnel, including standards for covert test data, quarterly reviews, and required corrective training for anyone who fails a covert test. Within 180 days, the agency would assess whether to replace or upgrade its system for tracking guard availability, and would create a plan and procedures for notifying building tenants about staffing absences or coverage gaps. The agency would report to Congress on these steps as they are completed and in annual updates.

hr-3486.one_sentence: The bill would increase criminal penalties for certain non-U.S. nationals who illegally enter or reenter the United States, including some who later commit felonies.
hr-3486.short: The bill sets a mandatory minimum prison term of 5 years, with a life sentence allowed, for a non-U.S. national who improperly enters or attempts to enter the country and is later convicted of a felony. It raises the maximum prison term for repeated improper entry from 2 years to 5 years. For people who were previously denied entry or removed and then enter or attempt to enter again without approval, it raises the maximum term from 2 years to 10 years, or to 15 years if they had three or more specified misdemeanor convictions before removal. It also sets a mandatory minimum of 10 years, with a life sentence allowed, for those with a prior felony or at least two prior illegal reentry convictions who again enter or try to enter.

hr-3492.one_sentence: The bill would make it a federal crime to provide certain gender-transition procedures or medications to minors and would broaden the existing federal ban on female genital mutilation.
hr-3492.short: The bill creates federal criminal offenses for knowingly performing or providing procedures or medications, such as hormonal treatments, to a minor to change the minor's body to correspond to a sex different from the minor's biological sex. Exceptions apply to specified procedures, including those treating individuals with both ovarian and testicular tissue or abnormal sex chromosome structure or hormones, and those treating infections or harms from a prior gender-transition procedure. A violation would be punishable by a fine, up to 10 years in prison, or both, and the bill bars arresting or prosecuting individuals who undergo these procedures or medications. The bill also expands the existing federal female genital mutilation ban so that anyone, not only a parent, guardian, or caretaker, who facilitates or consents to such procedures on a minor can be liable, while keeping the same penalties.

hr-35.one_sentence: The bill would create federal crimes for fleeing from Border Patrol or certain other law enforcement officers in a motor vehicle within 100 miles of the U.S. border.
hr-35.short: The measure establishes new federal criminal offenses for operating a motor vehicle within 100 miles of the U.S. border while fleeing from a U.S. Border Patrol agent or from a federal, state, or local officer actively assisting or under Border Patrol command. It sets criminal penalties for these offenses, including a mandatory minimum prison term when the offense results in death or serious bodily injury. A non-U.S. national who is convicted of or admits to committing such an offense would be inadmissible, deportable, and ineligible for immigration relief, including asylum.

hr-359.one_sentence: The bill would require the Department of Energy to report on how it uses its authority to reduce or waive required non-federal cost-sharing for federally funded energy research and commercialization projects.
hr-359.short: The bill directs the Department of Energy to report on its use of authority to reduce or eliminate non-federal cost-sharing requirements for federally funded energy projects. These projects cover research, development, demonstration, and commercial application activities under the Energy Policy Act of 2005. The first report would be due within 120 days of enactment, and reports would continue at least quarterly afterward.

hr-36.one_sentence: The MEGOBARI Act would require the President to impose visa blocks and authorize property blocks on foreign persons, including certain Georgian officials, who undermine Georgia's security or stability or engage in specified corruption or intimidation.
hr-36.short: The bill requires the President to impose visa-blocking sanctions on foreign persons determined to be involved in actions or policies that undermine Georgia's security or stability, and allows property-blocking sanctions as well. Immediate family members who benefited from a sanctioned person's conduct are also subject to these sanctions. The bill separately requires visa-blocking sanctions on certain current and former Georgian legislators, party officials, and government leaders who knowingly engaged in significant corruption or violence or intimidation related to blocking Euro-Atlantic integration. The President must also determine whether any foreign persons have engaged in significant corruption in Georgia or acts undermining its security, for possible sanctions under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.

hr-3616.one_sentence: The Reliable Power Act would require annual reliability assessments of the bulk-power system and let FERC review certain federal power-plant regulations before they take effect when generation shortfalls are found.
hr-3616.short: The bill directs the North American Electric Reliability Corporation to conduct annual long-term assessments of the reliability of electric power in the bulk-power system. If that organization finds there is not enough electric generation to maintain reliability, it must notify the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, which then alerts relevant federal agencies. Agencies must send proposed regulations affecting generation resources to the commission for review and cannot finalize them until the commission finds they are unlikely to significantly harm the system's ability to supply sufficient energy.

hr-3617.one_sentence: The bill would require the Department of Energy to assess and work to secure supply chains for energy resources that are essential to U.S. energy security and vulnerable to disruption.
hr-3617.short: The bill directs the Department of Energy to identify critical energy resources, defined as resources essential to the U.S. energy sector whose supply chains are vulnerable to disruption. The Department would conduct ongoing assessments of these resources, including supply chain vulnerabilities, domestic production capacity, federal regulations, reliance on imports, and efforts by adversarial nations to exploit these markets. The Department would also help develop strategies to strengthen these supply chains, develop substitutes and alternatives, and improve technology for reusing and recycling the resources.

hr-3628.one_sentence: The bill would require certain state utility regulators to consider rules ensuring electricity remains reliably available over a 10-year period from qualifying generation facilities.
hr-3628.short: The bill applies to state authorities that regulate electric utilities using integrated resource plans, which project future electricity needs. These regulators would have to consider requiring utilities to include measures ensuring reliable electricity availability over 10 years, either by keeping reliable generation facilities running or by buying power from them. The bill defines reliable generation facilities as those that can run continuously for at least 30 days, have on-site fuel or contracted equivalents, can operate in emergencies and severe weather, and provide services such as frequency and voltage support.

hr-3632.one_sentence: The bill would let the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission order a power plant to stay open for up to five years when its retirement would make the electric grid unreliable.
hr-3632.short: The bill changes how the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission decides whether a power plant must remain open, allowing complaints from state commissions and transmission organizations. If the Commission finds that electric service is or is likely to become inadequate within five years, it may order a plant to stay open for up to five years, and it must set any compensation and how costs are shared. Plant owners would need to give at least five years' notice before retiring a unit, except in emergencies. Actions taken to comply with such orders would be exempt from federal, state, and local environmental laws and regulations.

hr-3633.one_sentence: The bill would create a federal framework placing digital commodities, meaning digital assets whose value relies on a blockchain, under Commodity Futures Trading Commission oversight.
hr-3633.short: The bill sets up a regulatory framework for digital commodities, which are digital assets whose value depends on a blockchain. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission would generally regulate transactions involving digital commodity exchanges, brokers, and dealers, including requirements for trade monitoring, recordkeeping, and handling of customer assets. To trade on an exchange, a digital commodity must either be on a mature or decentralized blockchain, or its issuer must file certain reports. The bill also exempts qualifying digital commodities from Securities and Exchange Commission registration if annual sales stay below a set amount and other conditions are met, while giving the SEC jurisdiction over certain related activities.

hr-3638.one_sentence: The Electric Supply Chain Act would require the Department of Energy to regularly assess the supply chain for electricity components and report its findings and recommendations to Congress.
hr-3638.short: The bill directs the Department of Energy to periodically review the supply chain for components used to generate and transmit electricity. The review covers supply trends and vulnerabilities, barriers to processing critical materials in the United States, and domestic policies that discourage investment in the supply chain. The Department must also identify emerging issues and recommend ways to secure and expand the supply chain, with the first report due within one year of enactment.

hr-3668.one_sentence: The bill would make the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission the sole lead agency coordinating environmental reviews of certain natural gas pipelines and LNG terminals, and limit how long authorization decisions can take after those reviews.
hr-3668.short: The bill speeds up environmental review for certain natural gas pipeline projects and liquefied natural gas import or export terminals under the Natural Gas Act. It makes the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission the only lead agency for coordinating those National Environmental Policy Act reviews, and other agencies must defer to its approved review scope. The Commission must invite and designate participating agencies by set deadlines and cannot set an authorization deadline more than 90 days after the environmental review ends. Applicants would not need a state water quality certification under Section 401 of the Clean Water Act, and agencies must consider data gathered by aerial or other remote means.

hr-375.one_sentence: The bill would require federal agencies to partner with Hawaii to research, control, and address Rapid Ohia Death, a fungal disease that affects ohia trees.
hr-375.short: The bill addresses Rapid Ohia Death, a disease caused by a fungal pathogen that affects ohia trees in Hawaii. It directs the Department of the Interior to work with the Department of Agriculture and Hawaii on control efforts, and asks the U.S. Geological Survey and the Forest Service's Institute of Pacific Islands Forestry to keep researching how the disease spreads. It also has the Fish and Wildlife Service manage ungulates such as deer in affected areas, with private landowners' consent, and provides Forest Service funding to limit the fungus's spread and restore native Hawaiian forests.

hr-3838.one_sentence: This bill sets defense policy and authorizes funding for Department of Defense programs, military construction, and certain Department of Energy and Maritime Administration national security activities for fiscal year 2026.
hr-3838.short: The bill sets policies and authorities for fiscal year 2026 across Department of Defense programs, military construction, and national security activities of the Department of Energy and Maritime Administration. It authorizes purchases and modifications of military items, sets research and development policy, and establishes active-duty and reserve troop strength levels. It also covers military health care and compensation, acquisition and contracting rules including those affecting small businesses, cyber and artificial intelligence matters, and nuclear security and defense environmental cleanup. Its stated aim includes modifying the defense acquisition system to deliver capabilities to the Armed Forces more quickly.

hr-3898.one_sentence: The PERMIT Act would narrow the Clean Water Act by redefining "navigable waters" to leave out waste treatment systems, certain dry features, converted cropland, groundwater, and other features the Army Corps of Engineers identifies.
hr-3898.short: The bill amends the Clean Water Act by changing the definition of "navigable waters," which determines which water bodies the law covers. Under the bill, the definition would exclude waste treatment systems, ephemeral features that flow only in direct response to precipitation, and prior converted cropland. It would also exclude groundwater and any other features the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers determines should be excluded.

hr-3937.one_sentence: The bill would require the Forest Service to sell about 14 acres of federal land in Wisconsin's Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, including mineral rights, to a local company at market value.
hr-3937.short: The bill directs the Forest Service to convey roughly 14 acres of federal land, including its mineral rights, in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest in Wisconsin, to Tony's Wabeno Redi-Mix, LLC, if the company makes an offer to buy it. The Forest Service must first complete an appraisal to set the land's market value, and the offer must be received within 180 days after that appraisal is approved. As a condition of the sale, the company must pay the market value plus all associated costs. The bill also requires the Department of the Interior to publish a review of federal permitting processes for developing stone, sand, and gravel on federal lands.

hr-3944.one_sentence: This bill provides fiscal year 2026 funding for military construction, veterans programs, agriculture and FDA activities, and the legislative branch, and sets rules for using those funds.
hr-3944.short: The bill combines three of the twelve regular fiscal year 2026 appropriations bills: one for Military Construction and Veterans Affairs and related agencies, one for Agriculture, Rural Development, the Food and Drug Administration, and related agencies, and one for the legislative branch. It funds activities including Department of Defense military construction and family housing, the Department of Veterans Affairs, the Department of Agriculture, the Food and Drug Administration, the Senate, agencies that support Congress, and several related and independent agencies. Funds for the House of Representatives are not included, as each chamber sets its own requirements. The bill also sets requirements and restrictions on how funds provided by it and other appropriations acts may be used.

hr-3978.one_sentence: The bill would direct the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to license future U.S. facilities that recycle spent nuclear fuel under a streamlined rule set for special nuclear material instead of the rules for production and utilization facilities.
hr-3978.short: The bill applies to domestic facilities that reprocess spent nuclear fuel in a way that does not isolate plutonium, turning it into materials that can be reused as nuclear fuel for electricity. It directs the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to license such future facilities under its regulations for special nuclear material. To do this, it excludes these facilities from the legal definition of a production facility. The licensing process under those regulations has fewer steps than the process for production and utilization facilities. The official summary notes that no commercial reprocessing facilities currently operate in the United States.

hr-4.one_sentence: The Rescissions Act of 2025 would cancel specified unspent federal funds previously provided to the State Department, USAID, several independent agencies, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.
hr-4.short: The act rescinds, or takes back, certain unobligated funds, meaning money that has been provided but not yet committed to specific uses. The rescissions were proposed by the President under procedures in the Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974, and they take effect only if Congress enacts them into law. Covered funds include State Department and international assistance accounts such as global health, migration and refugee aid, and development assistance, with a number of programs excluded, along with USAID operating expenses and funds for the Inter-American Foundation, the U.S. African Development Foundation, the U.S. Institute of Peace, and the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

hr-4016.one_sentence: The bill provides fiscal year 2026 funding for Department of Defense military activities, excluding construction, family housing, Army Corps civil works, and nuclear warheads, which are covered by other bills.
hr-4016.short: The bill provides appropriations to the Department of Defense for fiscal year 2026, covering military personnel, operation and maintenance, procurement, research and development, and revolving and management funds. It also funds other Defense programs such as the Defense Health Program, chemical agent and munitions destruction, counter-drug activities, and the Office of the Inspector General. Related agencies receiving funds include the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System Fund and the Intelligence Community Management Account. The bill also sets requirements and restrictions on how these funds may be used.

hr-4058.one_sentence: The bill would require FEMA to provide ongoing outreach and technical assistance to stakeholders about certain homeland security preparedness grants and to report on how their feedback is used.
hr-4058.short: The bill directs the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to provide outreach and technical assistance to public entities and other stakeholders before, during, and after awarding grants under the State Homeland Security Grant Program and the Urban Area Security Initiative, which fund protection against terrorist attacks. FEMA would also conduct annual surveys of public entities about these grants and report on how stakeholder feedback is incorporated into the programs. The Government Accountability Office and FEMA would be required to report to Congress on implementation of the bill.

hr-4090.one_sentence: This bill would direct the Interior Department to speed up and expand mineral mining on federal lands to address weaknesses in the nation's mineral supply chain.
hr-4090.short: The bill directs the Department of the Interior to identify and expedite priority hardrock mining projects on federal land that can be approved quickly. It also requires the department to find existing or proposed mines that could increase production, add byproducts, or recover minerals from tailings or coal byproducts. Interior would have to review and revise agency actions it considers burdensome to mining, recommend changes to federal law, and review state and local laws that impede domestic mining. The department would also report on the economic impact of U.S. reliance on mineral imports and prioritize geologic mapping.

hr-4216.one_sentence: The bill would require the State Department to review each year which defense items sold only through government-to-government channels could also be sold directly by U.S. companies.
hr-4216.short: The bill requires the Department of State to conduct an annual review of defense articles and services currently sold only through Foreign Military Sales, identifying those that could also be sold through Direct Commercial Sales. For each item, the review must compare how long each sales route takes, the effect on State and Defense Department workload, and the benefits to national security and competitiveness. The State Department must report the results to Congress within 30 days of completing each review.

hr-4219.one_sentence: The bill would give statutory authority to an Invasive Species Strike Team program in the National Wildlife Refuge System and require the Fish and Wildlife Service to report to Congress on its progress.
hr-4219.short: The bill would formally establish in law the Invasive Species Strike Team program run by the National Wildlife Refuge System within the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. The program operates teams in each FWS region that work with public and private partners to address invasive species and related conservation issues in and around National Wildlife Refuges. The bill also requires the Fish and Wildlife Service to report to Congress on the program's work and on progress toward addressing invasive species that pose major concerns to the environment, human health, or the economy.

hr-4294.one_sentence: The MAWS Act of 2026 would create a NOAA pilot program to buy invasive blue catfish caught in the Chesapeake Bay Watershed for use in pet food, animal feed, or aquaculture feed.
hr-4294.short: The bill directs the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to set up a pilot program that helps buy blue catfish, which are considered an invasive species in the Chesapeake Bay, from watermen and seafood processors. NOAA would make cooperative agreements with makers or processors of pet food, animal feed, or aquaculture feed, and would set a minimum price per pound that accounts for market factors, stakeholder feedback, and separate prices for fillets and byproducts. The bill also requires NOAA to work with nonfederal partners on estimates of blue catfish abundance in the watershed and to publish the first estimate before the pilot begins.

hr-43.one_sentence: Removes a requirement that Alaska Native village corporations transfer certain lands to Alaska to be held in trust for possible future municipal governments.
hr-43.short: Under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act, Alaska Native village corporations must transfer certain lands either to an existing village municipality or, if none exists, to the State of Alaska to be held in trust for a future municipality. This measure would remove that transfer requirement. It would also let a village corporation regain title to lands already held in trust by passing a formal resolution, with the residents of the Native village taking part in the decision.

hr-4305.one_sentence: The DUMP Red Tape Act would require the Small Business Administration's Office of Advocacy to keep running a Red Tape Hotline where small businesses can report burdensome federal rules and report on those reports each year.
hr-4305.short: The bill requires the Office of Advocacy within the Small Business Administration to continue operating and maintaining the Red Tape Hotline. Small entities can use the hotline to report the burden of complying with federal agency rules, guidance, policy statements, or other activities. The office must report each year to the SBA and Congress on the notifications it receives through the hotline.

hr-4371.one_sentence: The bill would require HHS to weigh additional safety factors when placing unaccompanied alien children, including secure placement for certain older children with gang-related ties and stricter checks on sponsors.
hr-4371.short: The bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services to consider a child's danger to self, danger to the community, and flight risk when choosing the least restrictive placement, which is currently optional. It requires secure placement for children aged 13 or older who have gang-related markings or tattoos or a history of gang-related arrests or criminal conduct. For potential sponsors, HHS must collect and share with the Department of Homeland Security information on all adult household members, including background and criminal records check results. The bill also prohibits placing a child with a sponsor who is unlawfully present in the United States.

hr-4405.one_sentence: Requires the Justice Department to publish its unclassified records related to the investigation and prosecution of Jeffrey Epstein in a searchable, downloadable format.
hr-4405.short: The act directs the Department of Justice to release unclassified records, communications, and investigative materials it holds about the Jeffrey Epstein investigation and prosecution. These include materials related to Ghislaine Maxwell, flight logs and travel records, and individuals named or referenced in the case, including government officials. The Department may withhold items such as victims' personal information and material that would jeopardize an active federal investigation, and must report to Congress within 15 days on what was released and withheld, summarize redactions, and list government officials and politically exposed individuals named in the published materials.

hr-4423.one_sentence: The bill would require the U.S. representative at the World Bank's International Bank for Reconstruction and Development to keep pushing for a pause on new loans and payments to Burma, unless the Treasury Department finds this is not in the national interest.
hr-4423.short: The No New Burma Funds Act directs the U.S. Executive Director at the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), part of the World Bank, to advocate for and vote in favor of a continued pause on disbursements and new financing commitments to Burma. The pause would continue unless the Department of the Treasury determines it is not in the national interest. The World Bank paused disbursements and new financing to Burma after a 2021 military coup there.

hr-4541.one_sentence: This bill extends and revises federal breast and cervical cancer screening programs run by the CDC, including grants to states and education for young women about breast health.
hr-4541.short: The bill reauthorizes CDC programs on breast and cervical cancer, extending the National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program through fiscal year 2030 and related young women's breast health programs through fiscal year 2031. The early detection program gives states grants for screening, diagnosis, and treatment for people with low incomes, no insurance, or limited access to care, and the bill gives states more flexibility in how they spend those funds. The bill also requires the Government Accountability Office to report to Congress on the program, including how many people it serves and barriers to getting screened. The young women's programs fund awareness campaigns, prevention research, and grants for services to young women with breast cancer or precancerous conditions.

hr-4544.one_sentence: The bill would require federal financial regulators to review and simplify the process for approving new banks and credit unions.
hr-4544.short: The bill directs federal financial regulators to review how they handle applications to form new depository institutions and credit unions, and to reduce the amount of information applicants must submit where practicable. It also asks regulators to examine how new institutions raise capital while keeping investor protections in place. On request, applicants would be assigned a caseworker and given a list of similar institutions willing to serve as mentors, and each regulator would develop a plan to engage states and stakeholders on the approval process.

hr-4553.one_sentence: This bill would provide fiscal year 2026 funding for U.S. Army Corps of Engineers civil works, the Bureau of Reclamation, Department of Energy programs, and several independent energy and regulatory agencies.
hr-4553.short: The bill provides FY2026 appropriations for U.S. Army Corps of Engineers civil works projects, including investigations, construction, flood control, and water infrastructure financing. It also funds the Bureau of Reclamation and Central Utah Project under the Department of the Interior. For the Department of Energy, it provides money for numerous energy, science, nuclear, and national security programs, as well as independent agencies such as the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The bill also sets requirements and restrictions on how these funds may be used.

hr-4593.one_sentence: The SHOWER Act would set a federal definition of showerhead for water-efficiency rules by adopting one from the American Society of Mechanical Engineers and require the Department of Energy to revise its regulations to match.
hr-4593.short: The bill gives statutory authority to a revised definition of showerhead used in federal water-efficiency regulations. It adopts the definition established by the American Society of Mechanical Engineers. It also requires the Department of Energy to revise existing regulations to reflect the new definition, which the official summary says would replace a regulatory definition rescinded under Executive Order 14264 issued in April 2025.

hr-4626.one_sentence: The bill changes how the Department of Energy sets and revises energy conservation standards for household appliances and other consumer products, adding cost and availability considerations.
hr-4626.short: The bill lets the Department of Energy amend appliance energy standards when needed rather than by a fixed deadline, and allows it to revoke or amend standards after a petition if they raise consumer costs, save little energy or water, are not technologically feasible, or leave a product unavailable to consumers in the U.S. It changes the criteria for setting new standards, including a new test for whether a standard is economically justified. It also requires disclosure of certain Department meetings with entities tied to China or the Chinese Communist Party, those that have produced or advocated energy-limiting policies, or those that have received federal funds, and bars new standards for distribution transformers. Finally, it permits certain new or amended energy and water standards for clothes washers and dishwashers.

hr-4638.one_sentence: The bill would make a non-U.S. national who is convicted of, or admits to, harming an animal used in law enforcement inadmissible to and deportable from the United States.
hr-4638.short: The bill, titled the Federal Working Animal Protection Act and also called the BOWOW Act, addresses harm to animals used in law enforcement. Under the bill, a non-U.S. national (referred to as an alien under federal law) who is convicted of an offense related to harming such an animal, or who admits to having committed one, would be inadmissible. The same person would also be deportable.

hr-4646.one_sentence: The bill would extend existing whistleblower protections to employees of HUD-funded contractors and grant recipients, including those working under contracts and grants signed before the law took effect in 2013.
hr-4646.short: Current law protects employees of federal contractors and grant recipients from reprisal, such as firing, demotion, or discrimination, for disclosing evidence of certain misconduct involving federal funds to Congress or other appropriate officials. That protection applies only to contracts and grants signed or modified after 2013. This bill would extend the protection to all contracts and grants funded by the Department of Housing and Urban Development, regardless of when they were signed.

hr-4690.one_sentence: The bill would repeal energy efficiency standards that phase out fossil fuel use in new federal buildings and major renovations by fiscal year 2030.
hr-4690.short: The bill removes the requirement that new federal buildings and buildings undergoing major renovations phase out fossil fuel use by fiscal year 2030. It directs the Department of Energy to apply the standards as if that phase-out had never taken effect, until it issues regulations with revised performance standards. It also states that green building certification systems may not bar federal buildings from certification solely because they use fossil fuels directly or indirectly.

hr-471.one_sentence: The Fix Our Forests Act would set rules for managing federal forests to reduce wildfire threats, speed up environmental reviews of certain forest projects, and limit some lawsuits over those projects.
hr-471.short: The bill designates high-risk wildfire areas as fireshed management areas and creates an interagency Fireshed Center to assess and predict fire, including a public online registry of these areas. It speeds up environmental reviews for certain forest management projects, exempts some activities from those reviews, and creates intra-agency strike teams to coordinate reviews under several federal laws. The bill also limits certain lawsuits and court remedies involving fireshed projects, and it supports community wildfire protection, forest restoration, biochar demonstration projects, wildfire technology, and assistance for wildland firefighters and their families.

hr-4758.one_sentence: The Homeowner Energy Freedom Act would repeal three Department of Energy home energy programs and cancel their unused funding.
hr-4758.short: The bill repeals a Department of Energy rebate program for electrification projects in low- and moderate-income homes, state-based grants for training home energy efficiency contractors, and assistance to states and localities for adopting certain building energy codes. It also rescinds any unobligated funds available for the rebates and for adopting those building codes. According to the summary, funds for the contractor training grants were already rescinded by the 2025 reconciliation act.

hr-4776.one_sentence: The SPEED Act would narrow the environmental review requirements of the National Environmental Policy Act and speed up the review process for federal projects.
hr-4776.short: The bill limits which federal actions must undergo environmental review under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969. It states that federal funding alone does not make an action a major federal action, and it excludes actions already reviewed under certain other environmental laws. Agencies would consider only effects proximately caused by the project under review, and the bill also limits judicial review of NEPA cases.

hr-4795.one_sentence: The bill would bar colleges that receive federal student aid from boycotting Israel, and require certain federally funded schools to annually certify equal access to Israel-related academic programs.
hr-4795.short: The bill prohibits institutions of higher education that participate in federal student aid programs from taking commercial actions meant to limit business relations with Israel or Israeli entities, unless based on a valid business reason. Schools that receive or apply for Title VI funds, which support foreign language and international education programs, would have to certify each year that students and faculty can join programs located in Israel on the same terms as programs in other countries. They would also have to certify that students and faculty from Israeli postsecondary institutions can join their academic programs on the same terms as those from other foreign countries.

hr-4922.one_sentence: The bill would limit the District of Columbia government's power to change criminal sentences, lower the youth offender age limit from 24 to 18, and require monthly public reporting of youth offender crime data.
hr-4922.short: The bill would remove the District of Columbia government's authority to change any criminal sentence already in effect when the bill is enacted. It would also lower the maximum age for youth offender treatment from 24 to 18 and end a court option to impose sentences below mandatory minimums for youth offenders. Finally, it would require the D.C. Attorney General's office to publish and update youth offender crime data monthly on a public website.

hr-495.one_sentence: The bill would require U.S. Customs and Border Protection to report every year on how it is carrying out its plan to counter illegal cross-border tunnels.
hr-495.short: The Subterranean Border Defense Act changes the reporting requirement for a strategic plan against illicit cross-border tunnel operations. Under current law, U.S. Customs and Border Protection must report on the plan only once, within one year after the plan is developed. The bill would instead require recurring annual reports on how the plan is being implemented.

hr-498.one_sentence: The bill would bar federal Medicaid payment for certain gender transition procedures for people under 18, with some exceptions.
hr-498.short: The bill prohibits federal Medicaid funds from paying for gender transition procedures for individuals under age 18. It defines these procedures as surgeries, implants, and medications, such as hormones, intended to change a body so it no longer corresponds to the person's biological sex. Procedures are excluded if they are given with parental or guardian consent and aim to correct early puberty, genetic disorders, or chromosomal abnormalities, reverse a prior gender transition procedure, or prevent imminent death or impairment of a major bodily function.

hr-504.one_sentence: The bill would expand the Miccosukee Reserved Area to include part of Everglades National Park known as Osceola Camp and require protection of its structures from flooding.
hr-504.short: The bill adds a portion of Everglades National Park in Florida, known as Osceola Camp, to the Miccosukee Reserved Area. It directs the Department of the Interior, in consultation with the Miccosukee Tribe of Indians, to take appropriate actions to protect structures within Osceola Camp from flooding.

hr-5103.one_sentence: The bill would create a federal commission to advise on certain crime and immigration matters in D.C. and set up a federal program to keep commonly visited D.C. areas clean and maintained.
hr-5103.short: The bill creates a commission made up of representatives from U.S. Attorneys' Offices for D.C., Maryland, and Virginia, along with specified federal agencies and entities. The commission must recommend actions on matters such as enforcing federal immigration law in D.C., providing federal resources to reduce crime, and helping recruit and retain Metropolitan Police Department officers. The bill also directs the Department of the Interior to run a program to clean and maintain commonly visited areas like monuments, parks, and roads, and to restore damaged or removed federal monuments. The bill's provisions end on January 2, 2029.

hr-5107.one_sentence: The bill would repeal a 2022 District of Columbia police and justice reform law and restore the laws that law had changed.
hr-5107.short: The Common-Sense Law Enforcement and Accountability Now in DC Act, or CLEAN DC Act, would repeal the Comprehensive Policing and Justice Reform Amendment Act of 2022, which the Council of the District of Columbia enacted. Under the bill, any provisions of law that the 2022 act amended or repealed would be restored as if the 2022 act had never been enacted. The 2022 act covered policing measures, including limits on certain neck restraints by officers, additional procedures for body-worn cameras, and expanded access to police disciplinary records.

hr-5125.one_sentence: The bill would abolish the D.C. Judicial Nomination Commission and have the President, rather than the commission, appoint the chief judges of D.C.'s Superior Court and Court of Appeals.
hr-5125.short: Under current law, a commission recommends nominees for judges on D.C.'s Superior Court and Court of Appeals, and the Senate must confirm them. The commission also selects the chief judges of those courts. This bill would end the commission's role in judicial nominations. It would instead require the President to appoint the chief judges.

hr-5140.one_sentence: This bill would lower, from 16 to 14, the minimum age at which a minor charged with certain serious offenses in the District of Columbia can be tried as an adult.
hr-5140.short: Under current District of Columbia law, a person under 18 is generally tried as a juvenile, but a person 16 or older can be tried as an adult for offenses such as murder, first-degree sexual abuse, first-degree burglary, armed robbery, or assault with intent to commit those offenses. A person 15 or older can also be tried as an adult for a felony if it is in the public welfare interest and there are no reasonable prospects for rehabilitation. This bill lowers the minimum age for trial as an adult in these cases to 14.

hr-5143.one_sentence: The bill would repeal current limits on police chases in Washington, D.C., and generally require officers to pursue fleeing vehicles unless specific exceptions apply.
hr-5143.short: The bill would remove the current D.C. restrictions on when police may begin a vehicle pursuit of a fleeing suspect. Under current law, a chase is generally allowed only for certain serious crimes or threats, and only when other options have been exhausted. Under the bill, officers would generally be required to pursue unless the officer or a higher-ranking officer reasonably believes the pursuit would be futile, would create an unacceptable risk of harm to someone other than the suspect, or that the suspect can be caught more effectively by other means. The bill also directs the Department of Justice to report to Congress on the costs and benefits of D.C. police adopting technology that alerts the public to an active pursuit nearby.

hr-517.one_sentence: The bill would let the IRS postpone federal tax deadlines for people affected by a state-declared disaster when a governor requests it, and would lengthen certain automatic deadline extensions.
hr-517.short: The Filing Relief for Natural Disasters Act would allow the Internal Revenue Service to postpone federal tax deadlines for taxpayers affected by a qualified state-declared disaster, such as a natural catastrophe, fire, flood, or explosion, upon written request by a state's governor or the District of Columbia mayor. Currently, such postponements are available only for federally declared disasters. The bill also increases the automatic extension of federal tax deadlines for certain taxpayers, including relief workers, people killed or injured in a federally declared disaster, and those whose residence, business, or tax records are in a disaster area, from 60 days to 120 days.

hr-5184.one_sentence: The bill would cancel a 2022 Department of Energy rule on energy efficiency for manufactured homes and limit DOE's future role to making recommendations to HUD.
hr-5184.short: The bill would rescind a May 31, 2022 Department of Energy final rule setting energy conservation standards for manufactured housing. It would also remove DOE's authority to issue similar regulations in the future. Instead, DOE could offer recommendations to the Department of Housing and Urban Development on revising those standards, and the recommendations would have to meet criteria set out in the bill, including a determination of cost-effectiveness.

hr-5200.one_sentence: The Emergency Reporting Act would require the FCC to study 9-1-1 outages and hold annual public hearings and issue reports on major communications disruptions during disasters.
hr-5200.short: The bill directs the Federal Communications Commission to examine 9-1-1 outages that current rules do not require providers to report, and to consider whether visual information should be included in outage notifications. It also requires the FCC to recommend rule changes based on its findings. For any event that keeps the Disaster Information Reporting System activated for at least a week, the FCC must hold an annual public hearing and publish a report on the outages involved and suggestions for making services more resilient.

hr-5201.one_sentence: The bill would require the FCC to publish a report on how well multiline telephone system makers and vendors comply with Kari's Law, which requires direct 9-1-1 dialing.
