It states that Americans face greater risk each day DHS is subject to a lapse in appropriations. It also expresses gratitude to DHS employees for their commitment to protecting the United States.

hres-1131.one_sentence: This rule sets the House's procedures for debating four measures: a Homeland Security appropriations bill, a Homeland Security support resolution, a District of Columbia beautification bill, and a maritime vessel bill.
hres-1131.short: The measure is a House procedural rule that governs how four separate items will be considered on the floor. It covers an appropriations bill for the Department of Homeland Security for fiscal year 2026, a resolution expressing House support for that department, and a bill to create a program to beautify the District of Columbia and establish the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Commission. It also covers a bill amending federal maritime law on the types of vessels that may enter or operate in U.S. navigable waters or transfer cargo at U.S. ports. The official summary does not describe the specific provisions of the four underlying items.

hres-1140.one_sentence: This resolution sets the terms for House floor consideration of H.R. 5408, a bill that would speed up the time it takes for workers and employers to reach a contract under the National Labor Relations Act.
hres-1140.short: The measure is a House resolution that provides for consideration of H.R. 5408. According to the official title, that bill concerns accelerating workplace time-to-contract under the National Labor Relations Act. The available summary does not describe the specific provisions of H.R. 5408 itself.

hres-1156.one_sentence: This resolution expresses support for tax policies that help working families and recognizes tax relief enacted in the 2025 reconciliation act.
hres-1156.short: The resolution states that Congress supports tax policies intended to benefit working families. It also recognizes the tax relief included in the 2025 reconciliation act. The measure is a statement of sentiment and does not itself change any tax law.

hres-1174.one_sentence: This rule sets the House's terms for debating four measures: three bills amending the Clean Air Act and a resolution supporting tax policies for working families.
hres-1174.short: The measure is a procedural resolution that provides for House consideration of three bills, H.R. 6387, H.R. 6398, and H.R. 6409, each amending the Clean Air Act. The bills, as named in the title, concern air quality monitoring data affected by exceptional events or wildfire-risk mitigation, review by the Environmental Protection Agency of proposed legislation, and emissions standards for sources outside the United States. It also provides for consideration of H. Res. 1156, a nonbinding resolution expressing support for tax policies that support working families. The official material does not describe the specific changes each bill would make beyond these titles.

hres-1175.one_sentence: This resolution sets the terms for House floor consideration of H.R. 8035, a bill that would extend certain foreign intelligence surveillance authorities under title VII of FISA through October 20, 2027.
hres-1175.short: The official summary states that this House resolution provides for the consideration of H.R. 8035. The bill, as described in the official title, would amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 through October 20, 2027, and address other purposes. The available material does not describe the specific provisions of the bill or the procedural terms of the resolution beyond this.

hres-1182.one_sentence: This House resolution expresses support for rural communities across the United States and recognizes the House's work in the 119th Congress on policies affecting them.
hres-1182.short: The resolution states support for rural communities as environmental stewards, energy suppliers, providers of food and manufacturing capacity, and contributors to national economic stability. According to the official summary, it notes House policies related to energy, health care, manufacturing, and broadband connectivity in rural areas. The measure recognizes the work of the House of Representatives in the 119th Congress in supporting these communities.

hres-1189.one_sentence: This is a House procedural resolution that would set the terms for floor consideration of three bills on federal building energy standards, endangered species, and geothermal drilling, plus a resolution on rural communities.
hres-1189.short: The measure is a rule providing for House consideration of several separate items. It names H.R. 4690, which concerns repealing certain federal building energy efficiency performance standards, and H.R. 1897, which concerns amendments to the Endangered Species Act of 1973. It also names H.R. 5587, which concerns waiving a federal drilling permit requirement and exempting certain activities from the National Environmental Policy Act for geothermal steam, and H. Res. 1182, expressing support for rural communities. The official materials do not describe the specific provisions of these bills beyond their titles.

hres-1224.one_sentence: This resolution sets the rules for House floor consideration of several separate measures covering agriculture, school policies, the federal budget, military burial markers, and fuel standards.
hres-1224.short: The resolution provides for House consideration of five bills and one budget resolution. The bills concern Department of Agriculture programs through fiscal year 2031, parental consent requirements at certain public elementary and middle schools, a program to identify American-Jewish servicemembers buried under markers that incorrectly show their religion, and the ethanol waiver for Reid Vapor Pressure under the Clean Air Act. The budget resolution sets the congressional budget for fiscal year 2026 and budgetary levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035. The official summary provided does not describe the specific provisions of the underlying measures beyond their titles.

hres-1247.one_sentence: This resolution sets the terms for the House to consider H.R. 2102, a bill about veterans' disability pay and retired pay for certain disabled retirees.
hres-1247.short: The measure is a House resolution that provides for consideration of H.R. 2102. The bill itself would amend federal law on military retirement and veterans' benefits so that certain retirees with combat-related disabilities could receive both veterans' disability compensation and retired pay. The official materials provided do not describe the bill's specific provisions in further detail.

hres-1251.one_sentence: This resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter antisemitism, and honors Jewish-American contributions.
hres-1251.short: The resolution urges elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter acts of antisemitism. It honors the contributions of Jewish-American servicemembers. It also states a commitment to ensuring that all Americans, including Jewish Americans, can worship without fear of violence or persecution.

hres-1252.one_sentence: A resolution expressing support for law enforcement officers, recognizing their service and sacrifice, and offering condolences to the families of officers killed in the line of duty.
hres-1252.short: This congressional resolution expresses support for police officers and other law enforcement personnel across the United States. It recognizes the importance of ensuring officers have the equipment, training, and resources needed to protect their health and safety. It also honors the acts of sacrifice and heroism of the law enforcement community and expresses condolences and appreciation to the loved ones of officers who have died in the line of duty.

hres-1259.one_sentence: A House resolution expressing that the President should prioritize securing the release of five named people detained in China during future meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
hres-1259.short: The resolution states the sense of the House that the President should make the humanitarian release of Pastor Jin Mingri, Pastor Gao Quanfu and his wife Pang Yu, Dr. Gulshan Abbas, and Jimmy Lai, along with others unjustly detained by China, a priority in future engagements with Xi Jinping. It urges the President to seek verifiable proof of life, access to independent legal counsel, family communication, and medical care for these detainees. It also reaffirms U.S. commitment to defending political and religious freedom and to advocating for those detained for exercising those freedoms.

hres-1274.one_sentence: This resolution would remove a provision of House Resolution 1224 that required certain text from one bill to be included in another bill.
hres-1274.short: House Resolution 1224 contained a section that required the text of H.R. 1346, the Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act of 2025, to be included in H.R. 7567, the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026, commonly called the farm bill. This measure would make that section have no force or effect. The underlying resolution also provides for the House to consider both H.R. 7567 and H.R. 1346, and it was agreed to in the House on April 29, 2026.

hres-1275.one_sentence: This House resolution sets terms for floor debate on five measures covering cashless bail lists, bail fraud, court monitors, support for police, and FY2027 military construction and veterans funding.
hres-1275.short: The resolution provides for House consideration of five separate measures. Three address bail and courts: H.R. 5625 would direct the Attorney General to publish a list of states and local governments that permit cashless bail, H.R. 6260 would prohibit fraud in connection with posting bail, and H.R. 8365 would set conditions on courts appointing monitors. H. Con. Res. 96 expresses support for law enforcement officers. H.R. 8469 makes appropriations for military construction, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and related agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027.

hres-1300.one_sentence: This resolution sets the rules for House floor debate on three bills concerning veterans' records, veterans' benefit amounts, and a Smithsonian museum site, and waives a procedural requirement.
hres-1300.short: The resolution provides for House consideration of three separate bills: H.R. 1041, which would bar the Department of Veterans Affairs from sending certain information to the Department of Justice for use in the national instant criminal background check system; H.R. 6047, which would direct the VA to increase certain disability compensation and dependency and indemnity compensation amounts; and H.R. 1329, which would allow the Smithsonian American Women's History Museum to be located within the Reserve of the National Mall. It also waives a requirement of clause 6(a) of rule XIII concerning certain resolutions reported from the Committee on Rules.

hres-1333.one_sentence: This House resolution sets terms for floor consideration of four bills covering agriculture appropriations, child care funding, federal student aid fraud checks, and welfare block grant rules.
hres-1333.short: The resolution provides for House consideration of four separate bills. H.R. 8646 would make appropriations for Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and related agencies for fiscal year 2027. H.R. 7726 would amend the Child Care and Development Block Grant Act to withhold funds from noncompliant states, and H.R. 7892 would require the Education Secretary to use an identity fraud detection system to review each FAFSA. H.R. 8872 would amend the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program to target funds to low-income families, add program integrity safeguards, require measurement of improper payments, and set goals for reducing fraud and improper payments.

hres-1335.one_sentence: This House resolution condemns people who try to defraud the federal government and states the House's view that fraud-prevention reforms and pre-payment eligibility checks would help taxpayers.
hres-1335.short: The resolution condemns actors who seek to defraud the U.S. government. It states the House of Representatives' belief that legislative and policy reforms to prevent fraud and improper payments would improve the government's finances and benefit taxpayers. It also expresses the view that federal program eligibility and spending should be verified before payments are issued. The resolution is a statement of opinion and does not itself create or change any program or law.

hres-1336.one_sentence: This resolution lets the House consider certain Rules Committee reports on the same day they are presented, without the normally required two-thirds vote, through June 5, 2026.
hres-1336.short: The resolution waives a House rule that normally requires a two-thirds vote before a Rules Committee report can be considered on the same day it is presented. The waiver applies to any such resolution reported through the legislative day of June 5, 2026. The covered resolutions relate to a measure providing for reconciliation under title II of S.Con.Res.33.

hres-1345.one_sentence: This House rule sets terms for floor debate on four measures addressing federal fraud prevention, payment pauses, a fraud-focused inspector general, and a budget reconciliation bill.
hres-1345.short: The resolution provides for House consideration of four measures. H.R. 8312 would establish fraud prevention and program integrity functions and data sharing authorities within the Department of the Treasury and a permanent governmentwide Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery. H.R. 8464 would amend title 31 of the U.S. Code to authorize pausing and segmenting payments. H. Res. 1335 would condemn actors seeking to defraud the federal government and express the sense of the House on fraud and improper payment reforms and verifying program eligibility before payment. S. 2 would provide for reconciliation under title II of S. Con. Res. 33.

hres-1398.one_sentence: This is a House rule that sets the terms for floor debate on four measures, including defense and State Department funding bills and a Social Security disability demonstration reauthorization.
hres-1398.short: The official title and summary describe a resolution that provides for consideration of four separate items: H.R. 8800, which would authorize fiscal year 2027 Department of Defense, military construction, and Department of Energy defense activities and set military personnel strengths; H.R. 8595, which would make appropriations for national security, State Department, and related programs for fiscal year 2027; H.R. 8884, which would reauthorize demonstration authority for the disability insurance program under title II of the Social Security Act; and H. Res. 1383, which would commemorate the one-year anniversary of the enactment of the Working Families Tax Cuts. The materials provided do not describe the specific provisions, amounts, or effects of the underlying bills.

hres-1423.one_sentence: This House resolution sets up floor consideration of four separate bills covering daylight saving time, national security appropriations, veterans' benefits, and firearms retailer payment codes.
hres-1423.short: The resolution provides for House consideration of four bills: H.R. 139, which would make daylight saving time permanent; H.R. 8595, which makes appropriations for national security and State Department programs for fiscal year 2027; H.R. 9237, which would amend federal law to improve veterans' benefits and Department of Veterans Affairs administration; and H.R. 1181, which would bar payment card networks and covered entities from requiring or assigning merchant category codes that distinguish firearms retailers from general-merchandise or sporting-goods retailers. The official material does not describe the specific provisions of the four underlying bills beyond their titles.

hres-1438.one_sentence: This House resolution sets the procedures for floor consideration of several bills and a budget resolution, covering defense, Social Security disability, the federal budget, congressional stock restrictions, banking laws, and fiscal year 2027 funding.
hres-1438.short: The measure is a rule that tells the House how it will consider six bills and one budget resolution. The items include defense authorization for fiscal year 2027 (H.R. 8800), reauthorization of a Social Security disability insurance demonstration program (H.R. 8884), a congressional budget resolution for fiscal year 2027 (H. Con. Res. 113), and restrictions on stock holdings for Members of Congress and their families (H.R. 7008). It also covers improvements to federal banking laws (H.R. 6955) and continuing appropriations for fiscal year 2027 (H.R. 9770). The official summary repeats the list of items without describing the specific provisions of each bill.

hres-1486.one_sentence: This resolution would impeach President Donald Trump for high crimes and misdemeanors, based on one article alleging abuse of presidential powers.
hres-1486.short: The resolution would impeach President Donald Trump for high crimes and misdemeanors. It contains one article of impeachment concerning abuse of presidential powers. The article alleges that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and U.S. Customs and Border Protection were allowed to operate in violation of the First, Fourth, and Fifth Amendments while judicial oversight was undermined.

hres-1490.one_sentence: A House resolution that would condemn socialism in all its forms, oppose socialist policies, and call for passage of the SAVE America Act on elections.
hres-1490.short: The resolution states that the House of Representatives condemns and denounces socialism in all its forms, names the Democratic Socialists of America, and opposes implementing socialist policies in the United States. It reaffirms support for free, fair, and secure elections, calls for enactment of the SAVE America Act, and states that American elections are for American citizens only. It also recommits the House to upholding the U.S. Constitution.

hres-1498.one_sentence: This resolution would formally censure Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina, a formal statement of disapproval by the House.
hres-1498.short: The resolution would censure Representative Chuck Edwards of North Carolina. Its official title refers to allegations relating to him, but the available summary does not describe those allegations. The summary contains no further provisions.

hres-1499.one_sentence: This House resolution sets the rules for floor debate on four bills and one resolution, and on motions to suspend the rules; it does not itself change any law.
hres-1499.short: The measure is a procedural resolution that provides for House consideration of four items: H.R. 1501, which would add certain mineral production activities as a covered project under the FAST Act; H.R. 9436, which would extend the period during which certain regulations on the North Atlantic right whale remain in effect under the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023; H. Res. 1490, which concerns condemnation of socialism in all its forms; and H.R. 4795, which concerns eligibility for certain Higher Education Act funds for institutions connected to boycotts of Israel. It also addresses how motions to suspend the rules are considered. The provided material does not describe the detailed provisions of the underlying bills or resolution text.

hres-1530.one_sentence: This is a procedural resolution that sets the terms for House floor consideration of several bills and joint resolutions, without itself changing any law.
hres-1530.short: The official title and summary describe a resolution that provides for consideration of five measures: a bill to establish a National Fraud Enforcement Division at the Department of Justice, a bill on information-sharing between federal and state agencies to address fraud in certain federal programs, two joint resolutions disapproving Environmental Protection Agency rules on California engine and vessel pollution standards, and Senate amendments to a bill allowing early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction. The material does not describe the specific provisions of the underlying bills or resolutions, so it is not possible to say what those measures would do in detail from this text alone.

hres-161.one_sentence: This resolution sets the House floor procedure for three measures: two resolutions to disapprove federal energy and emissions rules, and a budget resolution for fiscal years 2025 through 2034.
hres-161.short: The resolution provides for consideration of H.J. Res. 20, which would nullify a Department of Energy rule on energy conservation standards for consumer gas-fired instantaneous water heaters. It also provides for consideration of H.J. Res. 35, which would nullify an Environmental Protection Agency rule on procedures for facilitating compliance with the waste emissions charge for petroleum and natural gas systems, including netting and exemptions. Finally, it provides for consideration of H. Con. Res. 14, which would establish the congressional budget for fiscal year 2025 and set budgetary levels for fiscal years 2026 through 2034.

hres-177.one_sentence: This House resolution sets procedural rules for floor debate on three joint resolutions that would disapprove of federal agency rules on appliance energy standards, rubber tire manufacturing emissions, and marine archaeological resources.
hres-177.short: The resolution provides for House consideration of three joint resolutions, each seeking congressional disapproval of a federal agency rule. The rules concern Department of Energy certification and labeling requirements for certain consumer products and commercial equipment, Environmental Protection Agency emission standards for rubber tire manufacturing, and a Bureau of Ocean Energy Management rule on protecting marine archaeological resources. The resolution waives all points of order against consideration of the measures and against provisions within them. It also limits floor debate to one hour and allows one motion to recommit before final passage.

hres-189.one_sentence: This resolution would formally censure Representative Al Green of Texas.
hres-189.short: The measure is a House resolution that would censure Representative Al Green of Texas. The official summary provided does not describe the grounds for the censure or any further consequences beyond the censure itself, so the material available is limited.

hres-313.one_sentence: This resolution provides for House consideration of a Senate amendment to a concurrent resolution that sets the federal budget framework for fiscal year 2025 and budget levels through 2034.
hres-313.short: The measure is a procedural resolution that sets the terms for the House to consider changes the Senate made to H. Con. Res. 14. That underlying concurrent resolution establishes the congressional budget for the federal government for fiscal year 2025. It also sets budgetary levels for fiscal years 2026 through 2034. The available summary does not describe the specific budget figures or policy provisions.

hres-352.one_sentence: This resolution calls on elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to condemn and counter antisemitism and to educate the public about the contributions of Jewish Americans.
hres-352.short: The resolution is a non-binding statement that urges elected officials, faith leaders, and civil society leaders to publicly condemn antisemitic acts and work against them. It also calls for efforts to educate the public about the contributions of the Jewish American community. The official summary does not describe any funding, enforcement mechanisms, or other specific actions beyond these calls.

hres-426.one_sentence: This House rule sets up floor consideration of two resolutions that would overturn specified federal agency rules and waives certain House procedural requirements for related budget resolutions.
hres-426.short: The measure provides for House consideration of S.J. Res. 13, which would nullify a Comptroller of the Currency final rule on business combinations under the Bank Merger Act, and S.J. Res. 31, which would nullify an Environmental Protection Agency rule on reclassifying major sources as area sources under the Clean Air Act. It waives all points of order against consideration of both resolutions. It also waives a House rule requiring a two-thirds vote to consider certain Rules Committee reports filed the same day, for resolutions reported through May 23, 2025, relating to Title II of H.Con.Res. 14, which sets budget instructions for FY2025 through FY2034.

hres-432.one_sentence: This House resolution sets up immediate floor consideration of H.R. 2550, a bill that would nullify an executive order limiting federal employee labor-management programs.
hres-432.short: The resolution provides for the House to take up H.R. 2550, the Protect America's Workforce Act, right away. The bill would nullify Executive Order 14251, issued March 27, 2025, titled "Exclusions from Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs." According to the summary, that order excludes specified federal agencies from requirements that generally apply to federal employees' labor organizing and collective bargaining, along with related management obligations.

hres-481.one_sentence: This House resolution condemns the rise in ideologically motivated attacks on Jewish people in the United States, including a June 2025 attack in Boulder, Colorado, and reaffirms the House's commitment to fighting antisemitism and politically motivated violence.
hres-481.short: The resolution condemns the June 1, 2025 attack in Boulder, Colorado, which it describes as a targeted act of terror and ideologically motivated violence. It also condemns the broader rise in ideologically motivated attacks on Jewish individuals in the United States. The resolution reaffirms the House's commitment to protecting Americans' rights to assemble peacefully and practice their faith without fear of violence.

hres-5.one_sentence: This resolution sets the rules the House of Representatives will follow during the 119th Congress, adopting the prior Congress's rules with specified changes.
hres-5.short: The resolution adopts the House rules from the 118th Congress with several changes, including limits on when motions to vacate the Speaker and motions to suspend the rules may be considered, and a ban on waiving the germaneness rule. It also bars consideration of measures exceeding a specified long-term budget impact as scored by the Congressional Budget Office. Other changes address committee procedures such as electronic voting and remote witness appearances, eliminate the House Office of Diversity and Inclusion and certain employee collective bargaining rights, and reauthorize several House committees and commissions. The resolution also provides for consideration of twelve listed House bills, H.R. 21 through H.R. 35, with some numbers omitted from the list.

hres-516.one_sentence: A resolution that would condemn the violent June 2025 riots in Los Angeles, California, and express gratitude to law enforcement agencies, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, for their response to recent demonstrations there.
hres-516.short: The resolution's official title says it condemns the violent riots that took place in Los Angeles, California, in June 2025. According to the Congressional Research Service summary, it also expresses gratitude to law enforcement agencies, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, regarding recent demonstrations in Los Angeles. The available material does not describe any further provisions.

hres-518.one_sentence: This resolution sets the procedure for House consideration of H.R. 2913, the Ukraine Support Act, and directs the Clerk to notify the Senate once the House passes it.
hres-518.short: The resolution provides for the House to consider H.R. 2913, the Ukraine Support Act. It also requires the Clerk of the House to send the Senate a message that the House has passed the bill, no later than one week after passage. The official summary does not describe the specific support measures contained in the bill itself.

hres-519.one_sentence: This resolution condemns the June 14, 2025 attacks on Minnesota state legislators, calls for rejecting political violence, and honors the victims and responding officers.
hres-519.short: The resolution condemns the June 14, 2025 attacks on Minnesota state legislators and calls on people across the United States to reaffirm their commitment to a safe, civil, and peaceful democracy. It honors Speaker Emerita Melissa Hortman and her husband Mark Hortman, who were killed, and Senator John Hoffman and his wife Yvette Hoffman, who were critically injured. It also recognizes the law enforcement officers who responded quickly and apprehended the suspected perpetrator.

hres-537.one_sentence: This resolution would impeach President Donald Trump for high crimes and misdemeanors, based on one article alleging abuse of presidential powers by usurping Congress's power to declare war.
hres-537.short: The resolution would formally impeach President Donald Trump for high crimes and misdemeanors. It sets forth one article of impeachment, which concerns alleged abuse of presidential powers. According to the official summary, that article charges that he usurped Congress's constitutional power to declare war.

hres-539.one_sentence: This resolution would formally censure Representative LaMonica McIver and remove her from the House Committee on Homeland Security.
hres-539.short: The resolution would formally censure Representative LaMonica McIver, which is an official statement of disapproval by the House. It would also remove her from the Committee on Homeland Security. The official summary does not describe the reasons for the censure or any further details.

hres-590.one_sentence: This resolution would have the House agree to a Senate amendment to H.R. 4, the Rescissions Act of 2025, and treat the bill as passed.
hres-590.short: The measure is a House resolution dealing with the Senate's changes to H.R. 4, the Rescissions Act of 2025. Under its terms, once the resolution passes, the House is considered to have agreed to the Senate amendment and to have passed H.R. 4. The official title refers to budget authority that the President proposed rescinding in special messages sent to Congress on June 3, 2025, but the available summary does not describe the specific funding affected.

hres-672.one_sentence: This House resolution sets the rules for floor debate on an energy and water appropriations bill and three joint resolutions that would disapprove Bureau of Land Management land-use plans.
hres-672.short: The measure is a procedural resolution that provides for House consideration of H.R. 4553, which would make appropriations for energy and water development and related agencies for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026. It also provides for consideration of three joint resolutions (H.J. Res. 104, 105, and 106) that would disapprove Bureau of Land Management rules covering the Miles City Field Office, the North Dakota Field Office, and the Central Yukon planning areas. The official material does not describe the contents of the underlying bill or the specific provisions of the land-use plans beyond their titles.

hres-682.one_sentence: This resolution sets the rules for House floor debate on two bills: one authorizing fiscal year 2026 defense spending and one increasing penalties for illegal entry and reentry after removal.
hres-682.short: The measure is a House resolution that provides for consideration of two separate bills. The first, H.R. 3838, would authorize appropriations for fiscal year 2026 for Department of Defense military activities, military construction, and Department of Energy defense activities, and would set military personnel strengths for that year. The second, H.R. 3486, would amend the Immigration and Nationality Act to increase penalties for people who illegally enter or reenter the United States after being removed. The official summary provided does not describe the specific provisions of either bill beyond their titles.

hres-713.one_sentence: This resolution would formally censure Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota and remove her from the Education and Workforce and Budget committees.
hres-713.short: The resolution would censure Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, which is a formal statement of disapproval by the House. It would also remove her from two House committees: the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on the Budget. The official summary does not describe the reasons for the censure.

hres-719.one_sentence: This resolution would condemn the assassination of Charlie Kirk and political violence in general, and honor his life and legacy.
hres-719.short: The resolution condemns the assassination of Charles "Charlie" James Kirk and all forms of political violence. It also honors Kirk's life, leadership, and legacy. The official summary does not describe any further provisions.

hres-780.one_sentence: This is a House procedural resolution that sets the rules for floor debate on H.R. 1834, a bill whose policy contents are not described in the provided material.
hres-780.short: The measure is a rule providing for consideration of H.R. 1834, which sets the terms under which the House will debate that bill. The official title refers to advancing policy priorities, but the provided material does not identify what those priorities or specific provisions are. Based on the available material, it is not possible to say what H.R. 1834 would change.

hres-873.one_sentence: This House resolution sets the terms for floor consideration of a Senate amendment to H.R. 5371, a bill providing continuing appropriations and extensions for fiscal year 2026.
hres-873.short: The measure is a resolution that provides for House consideration of Senate amendment S.Amdt. 3937 to H.R. 5371. According to the official summary, that bill is titled the Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026. The official material does not describe the specific funding provisions of the amendment.

hres-878.one_sentence: This House resolution would express the House of Representatives' disapproval of the behavior of Representative Jesús G. "Chuy" García of Illinois.
hres-878.short: The resolution is titled "Disapproving the behavior of Representative Jesús G. Chuy García of Illinois." According to the Congressional Research Service summary, it states that the House disapproves of García's behavior. The available official material does not describe the specific conduct involved or any further consequences.

hres-916.one_sentence: This resolution sets the rules for House floor consideration of six bills on college athletes' name, image, and likeness rights, Chinese government ties to schools, and small business regulation.
hres-916.short: The measure is a House rule that provides for floor consideration of six separate bills. The bills cover name, image, and likeness rights for student athletes, restrictions on elementary and secondary schools accepting funds or contracts from the Chinese government, parental notice of foreign influence in public schools, and limits on federal education funds for schools supported by China. Two further bills would address small business regulation, one setting the small business regulatory budget at zero and the other creating a Red Tape Hotline at the Small Business Administration for reporting burdensome agency rules. The official material provided does not describe the specific provisions of each bill in further detail.

hres-93.one_sentence: This resolution sets the procedure for the House to consider H.R. 27, the HALT Fentanyl Act, which concerns scheduling of fentanyl-related substances under the Controlled Substances Act.
hres-93.short: The resolution provides for House consideration of H.R. 27, known as the HALT Fentanyl Act, which amends the Controlled Substances Act regarding how fentanyl-related substances are scheduled. It waives all points of order against considering the bill, meaning procedural objections that could otherwise block it are set aside. The bill will be considered with the changes made by the House Rules Committee, as described in that committee's accompanying report.

hres-936.one_sentence: This is a procedural resolution that sets the terms for House floor consideration of six separate bills covering water pollution, investment funds, electricity supply, state power standards, natural gas reviews, and a veterans' burial.
hres-936.short: The official title says this measure provides for consideration of six bills in the House. The bills named concern waters of the United States under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, closed-end investment companies' ability to invest in private funds, reports on the electricity generation and transmission supply chain, a state consideration standard for reliable generation, interagency review of certain natural gas authorizations, and disinterring the remains of Fernando V. Cota from Fort Sam Houston National Cemetery. The available material does not describe the specific provisions of each underlying bill.

hres-939.one_sentence: This resolution would impeach President Donald Trump for high crimes and misdemeanors, citing two articles alleging abuse of presidential power.
hres-939.short: The resolution sets out two articles of impeachment against President Donald Trump. The first charges him with abuse of presidential power by calling for the execution of Members of Congress. The second charges him with abuse of presidential power by seeking to intimidate federal judges, which it says violates the separation of powers and judicial independence.

hres-951.one_sentence: This House resolution sets the rules for floor debate on six separate bills covering environmental review, hardrock mining, gray wolf protections, electric grid reliability, power plant retirements, and child trafficking.
hres-951.short: The measure is a resolution that provides for the consideration of six bills in the House of Representatives. The bills concern the National Environmental Policy Act, hardrock mining mill sites and an Abandoned Hardrock Mine Fund, removing the gray wolf from the endangered and threatened species list, reviewing regulations affecting the bulk-power system, adjusting Federal Power Act requirements and notice of electric generating unit retirements, and combating the trafficking of children. The official summary provided does not describe the specific provisions of the six underlying bills, so this resolution's own effects are limited to setting the procedure for their consideration.

hres-953.one_sentence: This House resolution sets the terms for floor consideration of four bills on health insurance, Medicaid funding for minors' gender transition procedures, penalties for genital mutilation and chemical castration of minors, and environmental review.
hres-953.short: The resolution provides for House consideration of four separate bills. H.R. 6703 concerns access to affordable health insurance. H.R. 498 would prohibit federal Medicaid funding for gender transition procedures for minors, H.R. 3492 would amend federal law on genital and bodily mutilation and chemical castration of minors, and H.R. 4776 would amend the National Environmental Policy Act to clarify provisions and make environmental reviews more efficient and timely.

hres-965.one_sentence: This resolution sets the rules for House debate on H.R. 1689, a bill that would require the Homeland Security Secretary to designate Haiti for temporary protected status.
hres-965.short: The measure is a procedural resolution that provides for the House to consider H.R. 1689. That bill would require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status, which allows eligible nationals of a country to live and work in the United States temporarily. The official summary does not describe further provisions of the underlying bill.

hres-977.one_sentence: This resolution sets the terms for House floor consideration of three bills concerning showerhead definitions, manufactured housing energy standards, and fiscal year 2026 appropriations.
hres-977.short: The measure is a House procedural resolution that provides for floor consideration of three separate bills. H.R. 4593 would amend the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to revise the definition of showerhead. H.R. 5184 would prohibit the Secretary of Energy from enforcing energy efficiency standards for manufactured housing, and H.R. 6938 would make consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026. The official materials provided do not describe the specific provisions of the three bills beyond these titles.

hres-988.one_sentence: This House resolution sets the rules for floor debate on five separate bills that would amend federal laws on retirement plans, overtime pay, tipped workers, and joint employers.
hres-988.short: The resolution provides for consideration of five bills in the House. The bills would amend the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 on how retirement plans may weigh pecuniary and non-pecuniary factors, and the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 on which activities count as hours worked, which child and dependent care payments are excluded from overtime rate calculations, and how a tipped employee is defined. A fifth bill would clarify when two or more employers are treated as joint employers under the National Labor Relations Act and the Fair Labor Standards Act.

hres-992.one_sentence: This resolution sets the terms for House floor debate on H.R. 7006, a bill providing further consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026.
hres-992.short: The measure is a procedural resolution that governs how the House will consider H.R. 7006, a bill making further consolidated appropriations for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2026, and for other purposes. The official summary does not describe the specific funding provisions contained in H.R. 7006 itself. The material provided is limited to the title and a one-line description of the resolution's purpose.

s-1003.one_sentence: Lulu's Law would require the Federal Communications Commission to issue an order explicitly allowing wireless emergency alerts to be sent to mobile phones when a shark attack occurs.
s-1003.short: Under current rules, authorized government authorities may send wireless emergency alerts about public safety threats such as severe weather, missing children, and other dangers to life or property. This measure would require the Federal Communications Commission to issue an order that explicitly permits such alerts to be sent to mobile phones in the event of a shark attack.

s-1020.one_sentence: The bill would let the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission grant hydropower licensees up to six more years to begin construction, and reinstate certain expired licenses.
s-1020.short: The bill applies to hydropower projects licensed before March 13, 2020. Upon a licensee's request, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission could extend the deadline to begin construction by six years beyond the eight-year extension already allowed under current law. That extension would come in no more than three consecutive two-year periods. The commission could also reinstate certain expired licenses for projects covered by these extensions, effective as of the date they expired.

s-1071.one_sentence: The bill would set policies and authorize funding and personnel levels for Department of Defense, Department of Energy national security, State Department, Coast Guard, and Intelligence Community programs for fiscal year 2026.
s-1071.short: The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 sets policies and authorities for defense and national security programs for fiscal year 2026. It authorizes procurement of items such as aircraft, ships, and missiles, sets active duty and reserve personnel levels, and covers military health care and compensation. It also includes provisions on defense acquisitions, relations with countries including Israel, Ukraine, and in the Indo-Pacific, cyber operations and artificial intelligence, military construction, and Coast Guard and State Department matters.

s-1318.one_sentence: The provided material describes a bill about foreign intelligence surveillance and central bank digital currency, but it does not match the stated title, so the measure's actual purpose cannot be confirmed from it.
s-1318.short: The official title refers to restoring the religious heritage of fallen servicemembers, but the attached summary covers a different subject. The summary says the bill reauthorizes Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act until April 30, 2029, and changes rules for certain searches of U.S. persons' communications under Section 702. It also prohibits Federal Reserve banks from offering financial products to individuals or issuing a central bank digital currency.

s-1383.one_sentence: The SAVE America Act would require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections and photo identification to vote in federal elections.
s-1383.short: The bill bars states from processing a federal voter registration application unless the applicant presents documentary proof of U.S. citizenship, listing acceptable documents such as a passport or a REAL ID-compliant card showing citizenship. States would also have to check their voter lists against the Department of Homeland Security's Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements system and remove identified noncitizens. The bill further prohibits election officials from giving a federal ballot to anyone without valid photo identification, allowing provisional ballots that must be followed by identification or a religious-objection affidavit within three days, and limits non-in-person voting methods to voters who submit a photo ID copy or meet other specified conditions.

s-146.one_sentence: The TAKE IT DOWN Act would make it a crime to publish nonconsensual intimate images, real or computer-generated, and require online platforms to remove them within 48 hours of notice.
s-146.short: The act prohibits publishing intimate visual depictions of adults without consent, or of minors with intent to abuse, harass, or sexually gratify, and also bans threats to publish such depictions. Violators face mandatory restitution and criminal penalties, including prison, fines, or both. Covered platforms, meaning public websites or apps that mainly host user-generated content, must set up a process for victims to request removal. Platforms must remove reported depictions within 48 hours of notification.

s-1582.one_sentence: The GENIUS Act would create a federal and state framework for payment stablecoins, digital assets that issuers must redeem for a fixed value, setting rules for who may issue them and how they must be backed.
s-1582.short: Under the act, only permitted issuers, such as subsidiaries of insured banks or licensed nonbank issuers, could issue payment stablecoins for use in the United States. Issuers would have to hold reserves on a one-to-one basis in liquid assets such as U.S. currency and certain Treasury securities, publish redemption policies, and report reserve details monthly. The act also sets rules for foreign stablecoin issuers, applies anti-money laundering requirements, and states that permitted payment stablecoins would not be treated as securities or commodities under federal law.

s-1596.one_sentence: The bill renames the Anahuac National Wildlife Refuge in Anahuac, Texas, as the Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge.
s-1596.short: The Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge Act would rename the Anahuac National Wildlife Refuge, located in Anahuac, Texas, as the Jocelyn Nungaray National Wildlife Refuge. The act would give statutory authority to Executive Order 14229, which had already made the same name change. The summary provided does not describe any other changes to the refuge.

s-2.one_sentence: The Secure America Act would provide about $70 billion through fiscal year 2029 to DHS, CBP, and ICE for immigration enforcement, border security, and related activities.
s-2.short: The act provides funding to the Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement through fiscal year 2029. Funds would cover hiring and training Border Patrol and ICE personnel, including child exploitation investigators, and purchasing border screening and surveillance technology. It also funds immigration enforcement activities, including agreements that let state and local agencies perform certain immigration functions. The act is a reconciliation bill, which Congress considers under expedited procedures that limit filibusters and amendments in the Senate.

s-2393.one_sentence: This act authorizes the Department of Veterans Affairs to carry out a major medical facility project in St. Louis, Missouri, during fiscal year 2026.
s-2393.short: The act permits the Department of Veterans Affairs to carry out a major medical facility project in St. Louis, Missouri, during fiscal year 2026. It sets a maximum amount that may be spent on the project. The project would include a new bed tower, a clinical building expansion, a consolidated administrative building and warehouse, a utility plant, and parking garages.

s-2403.one_sentence: The Retire through Ownership Act would let the fiduciary of an Employee Stock Ownership Plan rely on an independent expert's valuation of plan assets that lack a recognized market, if the expert follows specified methods.
s-2403.short: The act addresses how Employee Stock Ownership Plans, which are retirement plans where employees hold shares of their employer's stock, determine the value of plan assets. Under the act, a plan fiduciary may rely on a valuation from an independent valuation expert or business appraiser when the assets are not securities with a generally recognized market. The expert or appraiser must follow the methodology in IRS Revenue Ruling 59-60, which lists factors to consider when valuing stock of a closely held business.

s-2503.one_sentence: The ROTOR Act would require most aircraft to carry ADS-B In equipment, limit the military sensitive-mission exception to ADS-B Out tracking, and expand federal audits and aviation safety oversight.
s-2503.short: The bill requires most aircraft to operate with ADS-B In equipment, which shows pilots the location of nearby aircraft and provides traffic advisories. It narrows which flights can qualify as sensitive government missions exempt from ADS-B Out broadcasting, such as excluding training flights, and adds reporting requirements for that exception. It also repeals a 2025 law exempting certain military helicopters near Washington, DC from ADS-B Out requirements, and directs audits and reviews by the GAO, Transportation Department inspector general, and Army inspector general, along with new FAA coordination for military airspace use.

s-254.one_sentence: The ARTIST Act would stop states from banning the sale, trade, or possession of marine mammal ivory, bone, or baleen legally made by Alaska Natives into handicrafts and clothing.
s-254.short: The bill, also called Alaska's Right to Ivory Sales and Tradition Act, would prohibit states from banning certain marine mammal products made by Alaska Natives. Covered items include marine mammal ivory, bone, and baleen that are legally produced as authentic Alaska Native handicrafts and clothing. Under the bill, states could not block the interstate commerce, importation, sale, transfer, trade, barter, or possession of these items.

s-284.one_sentence: This bill extends the Congressional Award Board, which runs the Congressional Award Program for youth ages 14 to 23, through fiscal year 2028 and removes a requirement for the program's medal metals.
s-284.short: The Congressional Award Program recognizes young people aged 14 to 23 who meet set standards in public service, personal development, and physical fitness. This act reauthorizes the board that administers the program through fiscal year 2028. It also removes the requirement that program medals be made of gold-plated bronze, rhodium-plated bronze, or bronze. The reauthorization is effective as if enacted on October 1, 2023, the date a previous authorization expired.

s-307.one_sentence: The Prison Staff Safety Enhancement Act would require the Department of Justice to set national standards addressing sexual harassment and assault of federal prison staff by incarcerated people.
s-307.short: The act directs the Department of Justice to adopt national standards for preventing, reducing, and punishing sexual harassment and sexual assault committed by incarcerated individuals against Bureau of Prisons staff, including correctional officers. It also requires the Bureau of Prisons to fully implement the recommendations in a Justice Department Inspector General report evaluating how the Bureau addresses such incidents.

s-32.one_sentence: The Local Access to Courts Act would add College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, to the places where federal court must be held in their respective districts.
s-32.short: The bill adds College Station to the list of locations where federal court must be held in the Galveston Division of the Southern District of Texas. It also adds El Centro to the list of locations where federal court must be held in the Southern District of California.

s-331.one_sentence: The HALT Fentanyl Act would permanently place fentanyl-related substances as a class into Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act and apply the same penalties used for fentanyl analogues.
s-331.short: The act permanently places fentanyl-related substances as a group into Schedule I, the category for drugs with a high potential for abuse and no currently accepted medical use. Offenses involving these substances would face the same quantity thresholds and penalties as those for fentanyl analogues, such as a 10-year mandatory minimum prison term for 100 grams or more. The act also creates a new alternative registration process for certain Schedule I research and changes several research registration rules, including allowing a single registration for related sites in some cases. It further expresses the sense that Congress agrees with a 2018 federal court decision treating butyryl fentanyl as a fentanyl analogue.

s-356.one_sentence: This bill extends and modifies the Secure Rural Schools program, which makes payments to states and counties containing federal land for schools, roads, and related services.
s-356.short: The bill extends the Secure Rural Schools program, under which states and counties with certain federal land can receive payments from the Forest Service or the Bureau of Land Management for schools, roads, and certain other municipal services. It extends these payments through fiscal year 2026 and provides payments that lapsed for fiscal years 2024 and 2025. It also extends, through fiscal year 2028, the authority of counties to start projects using these funds and the authority to start projects proposed by resource advisory committees.

s-3971.one_sentence: The bill would extend and modify federal programs that give competitive research and development awards to small businesses, adding security risk reviews and other changes.
s-3971.short: The act reauthorizes the Small Business Innovation Research and Small Business Technology Transfer programs through fiscal year 2031, which fund research projects by domestic small businesses that could be commercialized. It requires federal agencies to evaluate the security risks of applicants, and to explain the basis if an application is denied for security reasons. It also caps how many proposals a small business may submit per fiscal year and expands training for contracting staff on commercialization awards, and it creates additional Phase II awards for critical technology areas for businesses that show effective technology and receive matching funds.

s-4465.one_sentence: This bill extends until June 12, 2026, the authorities in Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, which govern collecting foreign intelligence from targets outside the United States.
s-4465.short: The bill extends the authorities of Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) until June 12, 2026. Title VII generally covers surveillance and other methods of gathering foreign intelligence directed at targets outside the United States. It includes Section 702, which concerns acquiring communications of non-U.S. persons believed to be outside the United States. Information about U.S. persons may incidentally be collected this way and later searched under certain circumstances.

s-5.one_sentence: The Laken Riley Act would require federal detention of certain non-U.S. nationals arrested for specified crimes and let states sue the federal government over certain immigration enforcement decisions.
s-5.short: The act requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-U.S. nationals who are unlawfully present and have been charged with, arrested for, convicted of, or admitted to committing offenses such as burglary, theft, shoplifting, assault of a law enforcement officer, or crimes causing death or serious bodily injury. It also allows state governments to seek court orders against the federal government over specified immigration decisions or failures that cause them or their residents harm, including financial harm of more than $100. Covered matters include releasing a non-U.S. national from custody, certain inspection and asylum interview requirements, visa issuance for countries that unreasonably deny or delay acceptance of their nationals, limits on immigration parole, and failing to detain people ordered removed.

s-629.one_sentence: The act expands and revises federal emergency conservation and forest restoration payment programs for farmers and private forest owners hit by natural disasters.
s-629.short: The act changes the Emergency Conservation Program and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program, which help agricultural producers and owners of forest land pay for repairs after natural disasters. It allows advance payments for replacing, repairing, or restoring farmland and conservation structures, and for emergency work on private nonindustrial forest land, and gives recipients 180 days to spend the funds instead of 60. It also extends eligibility to certain wildfire damage, including fires not caused naturally that spread through natural causes and fires caused by the federal government.

s-723.one_sentence: The bill would set deadlines and notice requirements for the Bureau of Indian Affairs when it processes mortgages and related land documents on tribal trust land.
s-723.short: The bill requires the Bureau of Indian Affairs to notify lenders when it receives mortgage or right-of-way documents for tribal trust land, complete a preliminary review within 10 days, and approve or disapprove them within 20 or 30 days depending on the type. It also sets response times for certified title status reports and requires notice of processing delays. The bill gives federal agencies and tribes read-only access to the Bureau's Trust Asset and Accounting Management System, directs the Government Accountability Office to report on digitizing documents, and creates a Realty Ombudsman position within the Bureau's Division of Real Estate Services.

sconres-33.one_sentence: This concurrent resolution sets the federal budget framework for fiscal year 2026 and budget levels through 2035, and directs four committees to draft reconciliation legislation adding no more than $70 billion to the deficit.
sconres-33.short: The resolution sets out recommended federal revenue, spending, deficit, and debt levels for fiscal year 2026 and projected levels for fiscal years 2027 through 2035. It instructs the House Homeland Security and Judiciary Committees and the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and Judiciary Committees to submit recommendations by May 15, 2026, for legislation that would increase the deficit by no more than $70 billion over those years. It also creates reserve funds for certain reconciliation and immigration and border security legislation and sets budget enforcement rules for both chambers.

sjres-11.one_sentence: This joint resolution would nullify a 2024 Bureau of Ocean Energy Management rule that required archaeological reports for certain offshore oil and gas plans.
sjres-11.short: The resolution would cancel a Bureau of Ocean Energy Management rule, published September 3, 2024, that required oil and gas lessees and operators to submit an archaeological report with exploration or development plans for the Outer Continental Shelf. An archaeological report identifies material remains of human activity at least 50 years old. If the resolution is enacted, the Bureau would have to reinstate its earlier regulations, which required such a report only when a regional director had reason to believe an archaeological resource may be present in the lease area.

sjres-13.one_sentence: This joint resolution would cancel a 2024 Office of the Comptroller of the Currency rule that changed how proposed bank mergers are reviewed.
sjres-13.short: The measure would nullify a final rule from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, titled "Business Combinations Under the Bank Merger Act," published September 25, 2024. That rule changed procedures for reviewing applications for bank mergers. According to the official summary, the rule removes automatic approvals under an expedited review procedure and discontinues streamlined application forms.

sjres-18.one_sentence: This joint resolution would nullify a 2024 Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule that sets limits on overdraft charges at very large financial institutions.
sjres-18.short: The resolution would cancel the final rule issued by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, titled "Overdraft Lending: Very Large Financial Institutions," which was published on December 30, 2024. That rule concerns fees charged when a customer's bank account lacks enough funds to cover a transaction, known as overdrafts, at very large financial institutions. Under the rule, those institutions would have to cap overdraft charges at $5, cap them at a higher amount if they can justify it, or treat overdrafts as credit and follow the disclosure requirements of the Truth in Lending Act.

sjres-28.one_sentence: This resolution would nullify a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule that defines which payment app companies are subject to the Bureau's supervision.
sjres-28.short: The resolution would disapprove and nullify a final rule the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau published on December 10, 2024. That rule defines "larger participants" in the market for general-use digital consumer payment applications, meaning payment apps, that are subject to CFPB supervision. Under the rule, a nonbank company is a larger participant if it handles at least 50 million transactions annually and is not a small business concern.

sjres-31.one_sentence: This joint resolution would nullify an Environmental Protection Agency rule that requires certain facilities reclassifying as area sources under the Clean Air Act to keep using specified emission controls.
sjres-31.short: The resolution would overturn an EPA rule about facilities that move from the major source category to the area source category under Section 112 of the Clean Air Act. Under the rule, such facilities must continue using certain control methods so they do not increase emissions beyond the major source requirements in place when they reclassify. Area sources are subject to less stringent standards than major sources. The official summary states that the resolution would remove the requirement for sources of persistent and bioaccumulative hazardous air pollutants to comply with certain major source standards when they reclassify.

sjres-80.one_sentence: This joint resolution would overturn a 2022 Bureau of Land Management plan for the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska and restore the earlier 2020 plan, reopening portions of the area to oil and gas leasing.
sjres-80.short: The resolution would nullify a Bureau of Land Management plan issued April 25, 2022, for the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska, an area of roughly 23 million acres on the North Slope. The 2022 plan had closed about 48% of the reserve to oil and gas leasing to protect resources such as wildlife and subsistence use by communities. Under the resolution, those protections would be removed and the 2020 plan would apply again, reopening portions of the reserve to leasing.
